  • 2nd attempt: the server rejects authentication with error code 535.

docs.title: 16.6. The POP3 (Post Office Protocol) and IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) protocols
16.6.1. Introduction
docs.text:
There are two protocols for reading emails stored on a mail server:

  • the POP3 protocol (Post Office Protocol), historically the first protocol but rarely used today;
  • The IMAP protocol (Internet Message Access Protocol), which is newer than POP3 and is currently the most widely used.

To explore these protocols, we will use the following architecture:

  • [Server B] will be:
    • for POP3, the POP3 server of [Mailpit] (port 1110);
    • for IMAP, an IMAP server. This could be Gmail’s server ([imap.gmail.com], port 993), using the Gmail account and app password mentioned for the SMTP protocol. The results presented here were obtained using a local IMAP server, the open-source [Dovecot] server (https://www.dovecot.org), which has a user named [guest@localhost] with the password [guest]. We have placed the emails sent by our SMTP scripts in the user’s mailbox INBOX. With Gmail, you will get results in the same format;
  • [Client A] will be a client POP3 / IMAP in various forms:
    • the client [tcp-client.php] to discover the protocols POP3 and IMAP;
    • a PHP script that re-enacts the POP3 protocol discovered using [tcp-client.php];
    • PHP scripts that use the POP3 and IMAP classes, which we will write, followed by the library [zbateson/mail-mime-parser] to parse the messages.

The PHP 7 course used the functions [imap_*] from the [imap] extension of PHP, which supported both IMAP and POP3. This extension, which was based on a C library that had been abandoned for years, was removed from PHP 8.4. So we’re going to write the POP3 and IMAP clients we need ourselves, using the socket functions from PHP. This is an opportunity to gain a thorough understanding of these two protocols.

docs.title: 16.6.2. Exploring the POP3 Protocol
docs.text:
First, we use the [smtp-01.php] script to send two emails: one to [guest@localhost] and the other to [php8parlexemple@gmail.com] (the third attempt fails, as we’ve seen). The POP3 server of [Mailpit] displays all emails received by [Mailpit] in a single mailbox, regardless of their recipients. To read it, you must log in with a user from the [pop3-users.txt] file—in this case, [guest]—using the password [guest].

Let’s see how to access this mailbox using the [tcp-client.php] client:

> php tcp-client.php --quit bye localhost 1110
Client [127.0.0.1:47492] connected to the server [localhost:1110]
Type your commands (bye to stop):
<-- [+OK Mailpit POP3 server]
USER guest
<-- [+OK]
PASS guest
<-- [+OK signed in]
LIST
<-- [+OK 2 messages (682 octets)]
<-- [1 349]
<-- [2 333]
<-- [.]
RETR 1
<-- [+OK 349 octets]
<-- [Message-ID: <73n0AqT1QxqOYmrcWH5gK7@mailpit>]
<-- [Return-Path: <guest@localhost>]
<-- [Received: from vm (localhost [127.0.0.1])]
<-- [        by vm (Mailpit) with SMTP]
<-- [        for <php8parlexemple@gmail.com>; Thu, 1 Oct 2026 17:14:31 +0200 (CEST)]
<-- [From: guest@localhost]
<-- [To: php8parlexemple@gmail.com]
<-- [Subject: to gmail via localhost]
<-- []
<-- [line 1]
<-- [line 2]
<-- [line 3]
<-- []
<-- [.]
DELE 1
<-- [+OK message marked for deletion]
LIST
<-- [+OK 1 messages (333 octets)]
<-- [2 333]
<-- [.]
DELE 2
<-- [+OK message marked for deletion]
LIST
<-- [+OK 0 messages (0 octets)]
<-- [.]
QUIT
<-- [+OK goodbye]
Connection with the server lost...
End of the client
  • [php tcp-client.php --quit bye localhost 1110]: The server POP3 typically uses port 110. Here, it is port 1110 on [Mailpit];
  • [USER guest]: The command [USER] is used to specify the user whose mailbox you want to read;
  • [PASS guest]: The command [PASS] is used to set the user’s password;
  • [LIST]: The command [LIST] requests a list of messages in the user’s mailbox. The server responds with the number of messages and their total size, followed by one line of [number size] per message;
  • [RETR 1]: The command [RETR] requests the message specified by the number provided. The headers [From], [To], and [Subject]—sent by [smtp-01.php]—are included, along with headers added by [Mailpit]. [Mailpit] displays the messages from newest to oldest: message No. 1 is the most recently received;
  • [DELE 1]: The command [DELE] marks the message with the specified number as “to be deleted.” The message no longer appears in the list;
  • [QUIT]: The command [QUIT] tells the server that you are finished. At this point, the server deletes the marked messages. Both messages have disappeared from the [Mailpit] web interface.

The server’s response can take several forms:

  • a single line beginning with [+OK] to indicate that the client's previous command was successful;
  • a single line beginning with [-ERR] to indicate that the client's previous command failed;
  • several lines where:
    • the first line begins with [+OK];
    • the last line consists of a single period.

docs.title: 16.6.3. A basic script implementing the POP3 protocol
docs.text:
Since the POP3 protocol has the same structure as the SMTP protocol, the [inet/imap/pop3-01.php] script is a port of the [smtp-01.php] script. It has the following configuration file, [config-pop3-01.json]:

{
    "localhost:1110": {
        "server": "localhost",
        "port": 1110,
        "user": "guest",
        "password": "guest",
        "maxmails": 5
    }
}
  • lines 3–4: the POP3 server being queried is the server for [Mailpit];
  • Lines 5–6: the user and their password;
  • Line 7: a maximum of 5 emails will be retrieved.

The [pop3-01.php] script is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// POP3 (Post Office Protocol) client used to read the messages of a mailbox
// POP3 client-server communication protocol
// -> the client connects to the port of the POP3 server (110, 1110...)
// <- the server sends it a welcome message
// -> the client sends the command USER user
// <- the server answers OK or not
// -> the client sends the command PASS password
// <- the server answers OK or not
// -> the client sends the command LIST
// <- the server answers OK or not. If OK sends the list [no. size] of the messages
// -> the client sends the command RETR no. for each of the messages
// <- the server answers OK or not. If OK sends the content of the requested message
// -> the client sends the command DELE no. to delete a message
// <- the server answers OK or not
// -> the client sends the command QUIT to end the dialogue with the server
// <- the server answers OK or not
// the server's responses have the form +OK text or -ERR text
// The response may have several lines. Then the last one is made of a single dot
// the exchanged lines of text must end with the characters CR (13) and LF (10)

// the parameters for reading the mailboxes
const CONFIG_FILE_NAME = "config-pop3-01.json";

// we retrieve the configuration
$mailboxes = json_decode(file_get_contents(CONFIG_FILE_NAME), true);

// reading the mailboxes
foreach ($mailboxes as $name => $info) {
    // tracking
    print "Reading the mailbox [$name]\n";
    // reading the mailbox
    $result = readmail($info, verbose: true);
    // result display
    print "$result\n";
}
// end
print "Done\n";

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function readmail(array $info, bool $verbose = true): string
{
    // reads at most $info["maxmails"] messages of the mailbox described by [$info]
    // each message is deleted after being read
    // if $verbose=true, tracks the client-server exchanges
    //
    // opening a connection with the POP3 server
    $connection = @stream_socket_client("tcp://{$info["server"]}:{$info["port"]}", $errorNumber, $error);
    if ($connection === false) {
        return "Failed to connect to the server [{$info["server"]}:{$info["port"]}]: $error";
    }
    try {
        // after the connection, the server sends a welcome message that we read
        sendCommand($connection, "", $verbose);
        // USER command
        sendCommand($connection, "USER {$info["user"]}", $verbose);
        // PASS command
        sendCommand($connection, "PASS {$info["password"]}", $verbose);
        // LIST command: the 1st line of the response has the form [+OK n messages...]
        $response = sendCommand($connection, "LIST", $verbose, multiline: true);
        preg_match('/^\+OK (\d+)/', $response[0], $fields);
        $nbMessages = (int) ($fields[1] ?? 0);
        // we loop over the messages
        for ($i = 1; $i <= min($nbMessages, $info["maxmails"]); $i++) {
            // RETR command: the message is in the lines 1 to n-1 of the response
            sendCommand($connection, "RETR $i", $verbose, multiline: true);
            // DELE command
            sendCommand($connection, "DELE $i", $verbose);
        }
        // QUIT command: it is the one that deletes the messages marked by DELE
        sendCommand($connection, "QUIT", $verbose);
        return "Reading done";
    } catch (RuntimeException $ex) {
        // the server signaled an error
        return "Error: " . $ex->getMessage();
    } finally {
        // in all cases, we close the connection
        fclose($connection);
    }
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function sendCommand($connection, string $command, bool $verbose, bool $multiline = false): array
{
    // sends $command into the channel $connection and returns the lines of the response
    // verbose mode if $verbose=true
    // if $multiline=true, the response ends with a line reduced to a dot
    // throws a RuntimeException if the server signals an error
    //
    // sending the command if it is not empty
    if ($command !== "") {
        fwrite($connection, "$command\r\n");
        if ($verbose) {
            display($command, 1);
        }
    }
    // reading the 1st line of the response
    $line = readServerLine($connection, $verbose);
    // error?
    if (str_starts_with($line, "-ERR")) {
        throw new RuntimeException(substr($line, 5));
    }
    $response = [$line];
    // multi-line response?
    if ($multiline) {
        while (($line = readServerLine($connection, $verbose)) !== ".") {
            // a line of the message that starts with a dot was sent
            // with an extra dot: we remove it
            $response[] = str_starts_with($line, "..") ? substr($line, 1) : $line;
        }
    }
    return $response;
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function readServerLine($connection, bool $verbose): string
{
    // reads a line sent by the server and returns it without the characters \r\n
    $line = fgets($connection);
    if ($line === false) {
        throw new RuntimeException("the server has closed the connection");
    }
    $line = rtrim($line, "\r\n");
    if ($verbose) {
        display($line, 2);
    }
    return $line;
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function display(string $exchange, int $direction): void
{
    // displays $exchange on the screen
    // if $direction=1 displays --> [$exchange]
    // if $direction=2 displays <-- [$exchange]
    print match ($direction) {
        1 => "--> [$exchange]\n",
        2 => "<-- [$exchange]\n",
    };
}

Comments

As we mentioned, [pop3-01.php] is a port of the [smtp-01.php] script that we have already discussed. We will only comment on the main differences:

  • line 44: the [readmail] function is responsible for reading emails from the mailbox. The login information for this mailbox is stored in the [$info] dictionary;
  • line 51: Establishes a connection with the POP3 server;
  • line 57: Reads the welcome message sent by the server;
  • lines 59–61: the commands [USER] and [PASS] are sent to identify the user whose emails are wanted;
  • lines 63–65: the command [LIST] is sent to determine how many emails are in the mailbox. The function [sendCommand] now returns the lines of the response. In the first line of its response to the LIST command, the server indicates how many messages there are. This is retrieved using a regular expression. [$fields[1] ?? 0] returns 0 if the regular expression found nothing;
  • Lines 67–71: We loop through the messages. For each one, we send two commands:
    • RETR i: to retrieve message #i;
    • DELE i: to delete it once it has been read;
  • line 74: the command [QUIT] is sent to tell the server that we are done;
  • line 86: the parameter [$multiline] indicates whether the expected response has multiple lines, the last of which consists of a single period. This is the case for the commands [LIST] and [RETR]. An error is indicated by a first line beginning with [-ERR] (function [str_starts_with] from PHP 8.0);
  • Lines 110–112: As with SMTP, the server duplicates the period at the beginning of a message line. The client must remove this extra period.

We send two more emails using [smtp-01.php], then run [pop3-01.php]:

> php pop3-01.php
Reading the mailbox [localhost:1110]
<-- [+OK Mailpit POP3 server]
--> [USER guest]
<-- [+OK]
--> [PASS guest]
<-- [+OK signed in]
--> [LIST]
<-- [+OK 2 messages (682 octets)]
<-- [1 349]

<-- [.]
--> [RETR 1]
<-- [+OK 349 octets]
<-- [Message-ID: <67n1volg9CfPFES6KhEOf7@mailpit>]
<-- [Return-Path: <guest@localhost>]
<-- [Received: from vm (localhost [127.0.0.1])]

<-- [Subject: to gmail via localhost]
<-- []

Here we have a basic POP3 client that lacks certain capabilities:

  • the ability to communicate with a secure server;
  • the ability to read message attachments.

Before adding these features, let’s explore the IMAP protocol.

docs.title: 16.6.4. Exploring the IMAP protocol
docs.text:
The IMAP protocol is more feature-rich than the POP3 protocol. The server manages multiple mailboxes per user (INBOX, Sent, Trash, etc.) and tracks the status of messages: read, replied to, to be deleted... These statuses are called flags. Most importantly, the client can request the structure of a message from the server and download only a portion of it.

Each client command is preceded by a tag chosen by the client, for example, [A1]. The server responds with lines beginning with an asterisk [*], followed by a line beginning with the command’s tag, followed by [OK] (success), [NO] (failure), or [BAD] (invalid command).

Public IMAP servers accept only encrypted connections on port 993 from the moment they are started. With Gmail, you would launch the TCP client with the [--tls] option: [php tcp-client.php --tls --quit bye imap.gmail.com 993]. Our local server also accepts unencrypted connections on the standard port 143, which is useful for discovery. We sent two emails using the [smtp-02.php] script ([config-smtp-02.json] configuration), and they were delivered to the INBOX inbox of user [guest@localhost]. End of the client
  • [A1 LOGIN guest@localhost guest]: The command [LOGIN user password] authenticates the user. The server responds with a list of the user’s capabilities (CAPABILITY);
  • [A2 SELECT INBOX]: The command [SELECT] selects the mailbox to which the following commands will apply. The server lists the available flags (FLAGS), the number of messages (2 EXISTS), and the number of the first unread message (UNSEEN 1)...;
  • [A3 SEARCH UNSEEN]: The command [SEARCH] searches for messages based on a criterion. There are about twenty such criteria. Here, we are searching for messages that have not yet been read (UNSEEN). The server returns their numbers: 1 and 2;
  • [A4 FETCH 2 (...)]: The command [FETCH] requests information about a message. Here, it retrieves the message’s flags (FLAGS), its size (RFC822.SIZE), and four of its headers. The format [BODY.PEEK[...]] requests a portion of the message without marking it as read. The header text is sent as a literal: [{114}] at the end of the line indicates that the following 114 bytes are part of the response, regardless of their content (including line breaks). The response ends with a closing parenthesis after the literal;
  • [A5 FETCH 2 BODY.PEEK[1.1]]: Part 1.1 of message No. 2 is requested; here, its text is [text/plain]. We will soon see how the parts of a message are numbered;
  • [A6 FETCH 1 BODYSTRUCTURE]: We are requesting the structure of message No. 1, the one with five attachments. The response is a list of lists enclosed in parentheses. We can recognize the parts of the message that we saw in [Mailpit]: a list [(("text" "plain" ...)("text" "html" ...) "alternative" ...)] for the part [multipart/alternative], followed by a list for each attachment, including its type, parameters (name), encoding (base64), size, and layout (“attachment” with the file name). The structure ends with the [mixed] subtype of the entire message;
  • [A7 LOGOUT]: the end of the dialogue.

docs.title: 16.6.5. Classes for the POP3 and IMAP protocols
docs.text:
Our email-reading scripts will use either a POP3 server or a IMAP server interchangeably. We will therefore write:

  • an interface [MailClient] that describes what an email client can do;
  • an abstract class [TcpClient] that groups together what is common to both protocols: a TCP connection—which may be encrypted—over which lines of text are exchanged;
  • two classes, [Pop3Client] and [ImapClient], which inherit from [TcpClient] and implement the [MailClient] interface;
  • a class named [MimePart] that describes the structure of a message, obtained via the command IMAP [BODYSTRUCTURE].

They are located in the [inet/imap] folder:

imap
├── ImapClient.php
├── MailClient.php
├── MimePart.php
├── Pop3Client.php
├── TcpClient.php
├── config-imap-01.json
├── config-pop3-01.json
├── imap-01.php
├── imap-02.php
├── imap-03.php
└── pop3-01.php

docs.title: 16.6.5.1. The [MailClient] interface
docs.text:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// what a mail-reading client can do, whether it speaks POP3 or IMAP
// the messages are designated by their number (1, 2...) in the mailbox
interface MailClient
{
    // connection and authentication - returns the number of messages in the mailbox
    public function connect(): int;

    // the numbers of the unread messages
    public function unread(): array;

    // the main headers of the message no. $n (Date, From, To, Subject...)
    public function headers(int $n): array;

    // the full text of the message no. $n (headers and body)
    public function message(int $n): string;

    // marks the message no. $n as "to be deleted"
    public function delete(int $n): void;

    // deletes the marked messages and closes the connection
    public function close(): void;
}
  • Line 10: Connection to the server and user authentication. The method returns the number of messages in the mailbox;
  • line 13: the numbers of unread messages;
  • line 16: the main headers of a message, in the form of a dictionary;
  • line 19: the full text of a message, i.e., what we saw in the [Raw] tab of [Mailpit];
  • line 22: marks a message as “to be deleted”;
  • line 25: deletes the marked messages and closes the connection.

docs.title: 16.6.5.2. The [TcpClient] class
docs.text:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// base class of the POP3 and IMAP clients: a TCP connection, possibly
// encrypted (TLS), on which lines of text ended by \r\n are exchanged
abstract class TcpClient
{
    // the connection with the server (a resource of type stream)
    protected mixed $connection = null;

    // $info: the configuration of the server (server, port, tls, verify-peer, user, password...)
    // $tracking: if true, the client / server exchanges are displayed on the console
    public function __construct(protected readonly array $info, protected readonly bool $tracking = false)
    {
    }

    // opening the connection with the server
    protected function openConnection(): void
    {
        // connection encrypted as soon as it is opened (tls://) or not (tcp://)?
        $transport = ($this->info["tls"] ?? false) ? "tls" : "tcp";
        // should the server certificate be checked? (yes by default)
        $verify = $this->info["verify-peer"] ?? true;
        $context = stream_context_create(["ssl" => ["verify_peer" => $verify, "verify_peer_name" => $verify]]);
        $connection = @stream_socket_client("$transport://{$this->info["server"]}:{$this->info["port"]}",
            $errorNumber, $error, 10, STREAM_CLIENT_CONNECT, $context);
        if ($connection === false) {
            throw new RuntimeException("failed to connect to the server "
                . "[{$this->info["server"]}:{$this->info["port"]}]: $error");
        }
        $this->connection = $connection;
    }

    // sending a line to the server - $display: what must be displayed in tracking mode
    protected function send(string $line, ?string $display = null): void
    {
        fwrite($this->connection, "$line\r\n");
        $this->display("--> " . ($display ?? $line));
    }

    // reading a line sent by the server, returned without the characters \r\n
    // $display: should the line be displayed in tracking mode?
    protected function readLine(bool $display = true): string
    {
        $line = fgets($this->connection);
        if ($line === false) {
            throw new RuntimeException("the server has closed the connection");
        }
        $line = rtrim($line, "\r\n");
        if ($display) {
            $this->display("<-- $line");
        }
        return $line;
    }

    // reading $nbBytes bytes sent by the server
    protected function readBytes(int $nbBytes): string
    {
        $bytes = "";
        while (strlen($bytes) < $nbBytes) {
            $chunk = fread($this->connection, $nbBytes - strlen($bytes));
            if ($chunk === false || $chunk === "") {
                throw new RuntimeException("the server has closed the connection");
            }
            $bytes .= $chunk;
        }
        $this->display("<-- ... $nbBytes bytes ...");
        return $bytes;
    }

    // closing the connection
    protected function closeConnection(): void
    {
        if ($this->connection !== null) {
            fclose($this->connection);
            $this->connection = null;
        }
    }

    // display in tracking mode
    protected function display(string $message): void
    {
        if ($this->tracking) {
            print "$message\n";
        }
    }

    // analysis of the headers of a message: returns the dictionary [name => value] of the
    // decoded headers (non-ASCII headers are encoded, for example =?utf-8?Q?...?=)
    protected static function parseHeaders(string $headers): array
    {
        $dictionary = iconv_mime_decode_headers($headers, ICONV_MIME_DECODE_CONTINUE_ON_ERROR, "UTF-8");
        return $dictionary === false ? [] : $dictionary;
    }
}
  • line 7: the class is abstract; it cannot be instantiated. It serves as the parent class for the classes [Pop3Client] and [ImapClient];
  • Line 10: The connection to the server. The functions in PHP represent this as a resource, a type that cannot be declared in PHP: the type [mixed] is used;
  • Line 14: The constructor uses parameter promotion (PHP 8.0): the parameters [$info] and [$tracking] become properties of the class, in this case read-only ([readonly], PHP 8.1). The body of the constructor is empty. [$info] is the server configuration, read from a JSON file. [$tracking] requests that client/server exchanges be displayed;
  • lines 19–32: establishing the connection. If the configuration contains [tls: true], the connection is encrypted as soon as it is established (transport [tls://]). The context specifies whether the server’s certificate should be verified (entry [verify-peer], true by default);
  • line 36: sending a line to the server. The [$display] parameter allows you to display something other than what is sent: we’ll use it to hide passwords;
  • line 44: reading a line. If the server has closed the connection, an exception is thrown;
  • line 58: reads a specified number of bytes. We’ll use this for the literals in IMAP. The [fread] function may return fewer bytes than requested: we loop until we’ve received everything;
  • Line 91: The [iconv_mime_decode_headers] function parses a block of email headers and returns the [name => value] dictionary. It concatenates headers spread across multiple lines and decodes encoded headers (=?utf-8?Q?...?=).

docs.title: 16.6.5.3. The [Pop3Client] class
docs.text:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

require_once __DIR__ . "/TcpClient.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/MailClient.php";

// POP3 client: the commands USER, PASS, STAT, TOP, LIST, RETR, DELE, QUIT
final class Pop3Client extends TcpClient implements MailClient
{
    // number of messages in the mailbox
    private int $nbMessages = 0;

    #[\Override]
    public function connect(): int
    {
        $this->openConnection();
        // welcome message of the server
        $this->command("");
        // authentication
        $this->command("USER {$this->info["user"]}");
        $this->command("PASS {$this->info["password"]}", "PASS *****");
        // STAT: the response has the form [+OK nbMessages totalSize]
        $response = $this->command("STAT");
        $this->nbMessages = (int) explode(" ", $response[0])[1];
        return $this->nbMessages;
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function unread(): array
    {
        // POP3 does not remember the read messages: all the messages present are new
        return $this->nbMessages === 0 ? [] : range(1, $this->nbMessages);
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function headers(int $n): array
    {
        // TOP n 0: the headers of the message no. n followed by 0 lines of the body
        $lines = $this->command("TOP $n 0", multiline: true);
        $headers = self::parseHeaders(implode("\r\n", array_slice($lines, 1)));
        // LIST n: the response has the form [+OK n size]
        $response = $this->command("LIST $n");
        // we only keep the main headers
        $summary = array_intersect_key($headers, array_flip(["Date", "From", "To", "Subject", "Message-ID"]));
        return [...$summary, "Size" => explode(" ", $response[0])[2]];
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function message(int $n): string
    {
        // RETR n: the 1st line of the response is [+OK...], the following ones the message
        $lines = $this->command("RETR $n", multiline: true);
        return implode("\r\n", array_slice($lines, 1)) . "\r\n";
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function delete(int $n): void
    {
        $this->command("DELE $n");
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function close(): void
    {
        // nothing to do if the connection could not be opened
        if ($this->connection === null) {
            return;
        }
        try {
            // it is the QUIT command that deletes the messages marked by DELE
            $this->command("QUIT");
        } finally {
            $this->closeConnection();
        }
    }

    // sends a command to the server (if it is not empty) and returns the lines of the response
    // $multiline: does the response end with a line reduced to a dot?
    private function command(string $command, ?string $display = null, bool $multiline = false): array
    {
        if ($command !== "") {
            $this->send($command, $display);
        }
        // 1st line: +OK or -ERR
        $line = $this->readLine();
        if (str_starts_with($line, "-ERR")) {
            throw new RuntimeException("[" . ($display ?? $command) . "]: $line");
        }
        $response = [$line];
        if ($multiline) {
            // the following lines, up to the line [.], are not displayed in tracking mode
            while (($line = $this->readLine(false)) !== ".") {
                // the server doubles the dot that starts a line: we remove it
                $response[] = str_starts_with($line, "..") ? substr($line, 1) : $line;
            }
            $this->display("<-- ... " . (count($response) - 1) . " lines ...");
            $this->display("<-- .");
        }
        return $response;
    }
}
  • Line 9: The class inherits from [TcpClient] and implements [MailClient]. It is declared as [final]: no classes can be derived from it;
  • Line 14: The attribute [#[\Override]] (PHP 8.3) indicates that the method implements a method from an interface or overrides a method from a parent class. If this is not the case (e.g., a typo in the name), PHP reports an error;
  • lines 15–26: the connection. The commands from [pop3-01.php] are present here. The command [STAT] returns the number of messages and their total size on a single line. The password is displayed in the form [*****];
  • lines 30–33: the POP3 protocol does not keep track of read messages; all messages are treated as new. The [range(1, n)] function returns the array [1, 2, ..., n];
  • lines 37–46: The command [TOP n 0] returns the headers of message No. n followed by 0 lines of its body. The command [LIST n] returns its size. The function [array_intersect_key] retains only those headers whose names are keys in the array returned by [array_flip]. The operator [...] copies these headers into the returned array, to which the size is added;
  • lines 50–54: the command [RETR n] returns message No. n;
  • lines 64–74: The command [QUIT] deletes the messages marked by the command [DELE]. The connection is closed in all cases (block [finally]);
  • line 80: the method [command] is the function [sendCommand] of [pop3-01.php]. In trace mode, the lines of a multi-line response are not displayed; only their number is shown.

docs.title: 16.6.5.4. The class [ImapClient]
docs.text:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

require_once __DIR__ . "/TcpClient.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/MailClient.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/MimePart.php";

// IMAP client: the commands LOGIN, SELECT, SEARCH, FETCH, STORE, EXPUNGE, LOGOUT
// each command is preceded by a tag (A0001, A0002...); the server sends
// [* ...] responses then ends with a [tag OK|NO|BAD ...] response
final class ImapClient extends TcpClient implements MailClient
{
    // number of the last command sent (used to build the tags)
    private int $number = 0;
    // are there messages marked "to be deleted"?
    private bool $deletions = false;

    #[\Override]
    public function connect(): int
    {
        $this->openConnection();
        // welcome message of the server: [* OK ...]
        [$welcome] = $this->readResponse();
        if (!str_starts_with($welcome, "* OK")) {
            throw new RuntimeException("the server refuses the connection: $welcome");
        }
        // authentication
        $this->command("LOGIN " . self::quote($this->info["user"]) . " " . self::quote($this->info["password"]),
            "LOGIN " . self::quote($this->info["user"]) . " *****");
        // selection of the mailbox: one of the responses has the form [* n EXISTS]
        $responses = $this->command("SELECT " . self::quote($this->info["mailbox"] ?? "INBOX"));
        $exists = array_find($responses, fn(array $response): bool => ($response[1] ?? "") === "EXISTS");
        return (int) ($exists[0] ?? 0);
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function unread(): array
    {
        // the response has the form [* SEARCH n1 n2 ...]
        $responses = $this->command("SEARCH UNSEEN");
        $search = array_find($responses, fn(array $response): bool => $response[0] === "SEARCH") ?? ["SEARCH"];
        return array_map(intval(...), array_slice($search, 1));
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function headers(int $n): array
    {
        // BODY.PEEK[HEADER]: the headers of the message, without marking it as read
        $data = $this->fetch($n, "(FLAGS RFC822.SIZE BODY.PEEK[HEADER])");
        $headers = self::parseHeaders($data["BODY[HEADER]"]);
        // we only keep the main headers
        $summary = array_intersect_key($headers, array_flip(["Date", "From", "To", "Subject", "Message-ID"]));
        return [...$summary, "Flags" => implode(" ", $data["FLAGS"]), "Size" => $data["RFC822.SIZE"]];
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function message(int $n): string
    {
        // BODY[]: the whole message; the server marks it as read (\Seen flag)
        return $this->fetch($n, "BODY[]")["BODY[]"];
    }

    // the MIME structure of the message no. $n
    public function structure(int $n): MimePart
    {
        return MimePart::fromBodyStructure($this->fetch($n, "BODYSTRUCTURE")["BODYSTRUCTURE"]);
    }

    // the (encoded) content of the part no. $section (1, 1.2...) of the message no. $n
    public function part(int $n, string $section): string
    {
        return $this->fetch($n, "BODY[$section]")["BODY[$section]"] ?? "";
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function delete(int $n): void
    {
        // we add the \Deleted flag to the message
        $this->command("STORE $n +FLAGS (\\Deleted)");
        $this->deletions = true;
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function close(): void
    {
        // nothing to do if the connection could not be opened
        if ($this->connection === null) {
            return;
        }
        try {
            // EXPUNGE deletes the messages that have the \Deleted flag
            if ($this->deletions) {
                $this->command("EXPUNGE");
            }
            $this->command("LOGOUT");
        } finally {
            $this->closeConnection();
        }
    }

    // FETCH n items command: returns the dictionary [item => value] of the response
    // [* n FETCH (item1 value1 item2 value2 ...)]
    private function fetch(int $n, string $items): array
    {
        $responses = $this->command("FETCH $n $items");
        $fetch = array_find($responses, fn(array $response): bool => ($response[1] ?? "") === "FETCH");
        if ($fetch === null) {
            throw new RuntimeException("no message no. $n");
        }
        $dictionary = [];
        foreach (array_chunk($fetch[2], 2) as [$key, $value]) {
            $dictionary[strtoupper($key)] = $value;
        }
        return $dictionary;
    }

    // sends a tagged command and returns its [* ...] responses, each one split into tokens
    // $display: what must be displayed in tracking mode (to hide a password)
    private function command(string $command, ?string $display = null): array
    {
        $tag = sprintf("A%04d", ++$this->number);
        $this->send("$tag $command", $display === null ? null : "$tag $display");
        $responses = [];
        while (true) {
            [$text, $literals] = $this->readResponse();
            // final response [tag OK|NO|BAD text]?
            if (str_starts_with($text, "$tag ")) {
                $status = substr($text, strlen($tag) + 1);
                if (!str_starts_with($status, "OK")) {
                    throw new RuntimeException("[" . ($display ?? $command) . "]: $status");
                }
                return $responses;
            }
            // [* ...] response
            if (str_starts_with($text, "* ")) {
                $position = 2;
                $responses[] = self::tokens($text, $position, $literals);
            }
        }
    }

    // reads a response of the server: a line that may contain literals. A literal
    // is announced by {n} at the end of the line: n bytes follow, then the rest of the line.
    // returns the text of the response, where the literal no. k is replaced by \0k\0, and the literals
    private function readResponse(): array
    {
        $text = "";
        $literals = [];
        while (true) {
            $line = $this->readLine();
            if (preg_match('/\{(\d+)\}$/', $line, $fields) !== 1) {
                return [$text . $line, $literals];
            }
            $text .= substr($line, 0, -strlen($fields[0])) . "\0" . count($literals) . "\0";
            $literals[] = $this->readBytes((int) $fields[1]);
        }
    }

    // splits $text into tokens from the position $position, up to the end of the text or
    // up to a closing parenthesis. A list (...) becomes an array, NIL becomes null,
    // a string "..." or a literal becomes a string, everything else (atom) too
    private static function tokens(string $text, int &$position, array $literals): array
    {
        $tokens = [];
        $length = strlen($text);
        while ($position < $length) {
            $c = $text[$position];
            if ($c === " ") {
                $position++;
            } elseif ($c === "(") {
                // a list: recursive call
                $position++;
                $tokens[] = self::tokens($text, $position, $literals);
            } elseif ($c === ")") {
                // end of the current list
                $position++;
                return $tokens;
            } elseif ($c === '"') {
                // a quoted string where \" and \\ represent " and \
                $string = "";
                for ($position++; $text[$position] !== '"'; $position++) {
                    if ($text[$position] === "\\") {
                        $position++;
                    }
                    $string .= $text[$position];
                }
                $position++;
                $tokens[] = $string;
            } elseif ($c === "\0") {
                // a literal
                $end = strpos($text, "\0", $position + 1);
                $tokens[] = $literals[(int) substr($text, $position + 1, $end - $position - 1)];
                $position = $end + 1;
            } else {
                // an atom: up to the next space or parenthesis, except inside brackets
                // (BODY[HEADER.FIELDS (FROM TO)] is a single atom)
                $start = $position;
                $brackets = 0;
                while ($position < $length
                    && ($brackets > 0 || !in_array($text[$position], [" ", "(", ")"], true))) {
                    $brackets += match ($text[$position]) { "[" => 1, "]" => -1, default => 0 };
                    $position++;
                }
                $atom = substr($text, $start, $position - $start);
                $tokens[] = $atom === "NIL" ? null : $atom;
            }
        }
        return $tokens;
    }

    // an IMAP string: between quotes, with \ before the characters " and \
    private static function quote(string $text): string
    {
        return '"' . addcslashes($text, '"\\') . '"';
    }
}
  • Line 15: the number of the last command. It is used to generate the labels [A0001], [A0002]...;
  • Lines 20–34: The connection. The server first sends a welcome message: [* OK ...]. The commands [LOGIN] and [SELECT] are then sent. The [command] method returns the server’s responses [* ...], each split into tokens: the response [* 2 EXISTS] becomes the array [["2", "EXISTS"]]. The function [array_find] (PHP 8.4) returns the first element of the array that satisfies the condition, or [null];
  • lines 38–43: the command [SEARCH UNSEEN]. The result [* SEARCH 1 2] becomes [["SEARCH", "1", "2"]]. We retain the elements starting from number 1 ([array_slice]), which are converted to integers by the function [intval]. The notation [intval(...)] (PHP 8.1) creates a function from the function [intval]: this is the syntax for first-class callables;
  • lines 47–54: the command [FETCH n (FLAGS RFC822.SIZE BODY.PEEK[HEADER])] returns the flags, size, and headers of message No. n;
  • lines 58–61: the command [FETCH n BODY[]] returns message No. n in its entirety. The server adds the flag [\Seen] to it: the message is now marked as read;
  • lines 65–67: The command [FETCH n BODYSTRUCTURE] returns the message structure, which the class [MimePart] transforms into an object tree;
  • lines 71–73: The command [FETCH n BODY[section]] returns the content of part No. [section] of the message, as encoded in the message (Base64, quoted-printable, etc.);
  • lines 77–81: The command [STORE n +FLAGS (\Deleted)] adds the flag [\Deleted] to the message. It has not yet been removed;
  • lines 85–98: The command [EXPUNGE] deletes messages that have the flag [\Deleted]. The command [LOGOUT] ends the dialogue;
  • lines 104–115: The method [fetch] sends a [FETCH] command and converts the [[* n FETCH (item1 value1 item2 value2...)]] response list into a [[item1 => value1, item2 => value2...]] dictionary. The [array_chunk] function splits the list into pairs, which the [foreach] loop unpacks into [[$key, $value]];
  • lines 120–133: The [command] method sends a command preceded by its label, then reads the server’s responses until it finds the one that begins with the label. If this final response is not [OK], an exception is thrown;
  • lines 146–153: reading a response. If a line ends with [{n}], it is followed by n bytes (the literal) and then the rest of the response. In the response text, each literal is replaced by a marker [\0k\0] (\0 is the character with code 0, which cannot appear in a line of text IMAP) and its content is stored in the array [$literals];
  • lines 163–209: the method [tokens] splits the text of a response into tokens:
    • a list enclosed in parentheses becomes an array. The method calls itself (recursive call) to parse the list’s contents, and returns control at the closing parenthesis;
    • a string enclosed in quotation marks or a literal becomes a string;
    • [NIL] becomes [null];
    • everything else (an atom) becomes a string. An atom may contain square brackets, which themselves may contain spaces and parentheses: [BODY[HEADER.FIELDS (FROM TO)]] is a single atom. The expression [match] adds 1 to the open square bracket counter for [[] and subtracts 1 from it for []];
    • The parameter [$position], passed by reference, is the current position in the text: it advances as the analysis proceeds, including within recursive calls;
  • Line 213: A string IMAP is enclosed in quotation marks. The function [addcslashes] prepends a [\] character to the characters ["] and [\].

docs.title: 16.6.5.5. The class [MimePart]
docs.text:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// a part of a MIME message, as described by the BODYSTRUCTURE response of an IMAP server
// a message is a tree of parts: a [multipart/xxx] part has subparts
final readonly class MimePart
{
    public function __construct(
        // MIME type and subtype in lowercase: text/plain, multipart/mixed, application/pdf...
        public string $type,
        public string $subType,
        // parameters of the type, for example [charset => utf-8]
        public array $parameters = [],
        // encoding of the content: 7bit, 8bit, base64, quoted-printable...
        public string $encoding = "7bit",
        // disposition (attachment, inline) or null, and its parameters, for example [filename => x.pdf]
        public ?string $disposition = null,
        public array $dispositionParameters = [],
        // the subparts of a [multipart/xxx] part
        public array $parts = [],
    ) {
    }

    // builds the tree of parts from the list of BODYSTRUCTURE tokens
    public static function fromBodyStructure(array $structure): self
    {
        // multiple part: ((subpart 1) (subpart 2)... "subtype" (parameters) disposition...)
        if (is_array($structure[0])) {
            // the subparts are the first elements that are lists
            $parts = [];
            $i = 0;
            while (is_array($structure[$i])) {
                $parts[] = self::fromBodyStructure($structure[$i++]);
            }
            return new self(
                type: "multipart",
                subType: strtolower($structure[$i]),
                parameters: self::dictionary($structure[$i + 1] ?? null),
                disposition: self::disposition($structure[$i + 2] ?? null)[0],
                dispositionParameters: self::disposition($structure[$i + 2] ?? null)[1],
                parts: $parts,
            );
        }
        // simple part: ("type" "subtype" (parameters) id description "encoding" size ...)
        $type = strtolower($structure[0]);
        $subType = strtolower($structure[1]);
        // the disposition comes after fields that depend on the type of the part
        $dispositionIndex = match (true) {
            // text/xxx: ... size nbLines md5 disposition
            $type === "text" => 9,
            // message/rfc822: ... size envelope structure nbLines md5 disposition
            $type === "message" && $subType === "rfc822" => 11,
            // others: ... size md5 disposition
            default => 8,
        };
        [$disposition, $dispositionParameters] = self::disposition($structure[$dispositionIndex] ?? null);
        return new self(
            type: $type,
            subType: $subType,
            parameters: self::dictionary($structure[2]),
            encoding: strtolower($structure[5] ?? "7bit"),
            disposition: $disposition,
            dispositionParameters: $dispositionParameters,
        );
    }

    // the file name of an attachment, or null
    public function fileName(): ?string
    {
        // the name is the [filename] parameter of the disposition, or failing that the [name] parameter
        // of the type. It can be encoded in two ways:
        // - filename*=utf-8''Tah%C3%A9.png (RFC 2231);
        // - name="=?utf-8?Q?Tah=C3=A9.png?=" (RFC 2047);
        $encoded = $this->dispositionParameters["filename*"] ?? $this->parameters["name*"] ?? null;
        if ($encoded !== null) {
            // character set''URL-encoded name
            [$charset, , $name] = explode("'", $encoded, 3);
            return mb_convert_encoding(rawurldecode($name), "UTF-8", $charset);
        }
        $name = $this->dispositionParameters["filename"] ?? $this->parameters["name"] ?? null;
        return $name === null ? null : iconv_mime_decode($name, ICONV_MIME_DECODE_CONTINUE_ON_ERROR, "UTF-8");
    }

    // an IMAP list (key1 value1 key2 value2...) or NIL turned into a dictionary
    private static function dictionary(?array $list): array
    {
        $dictionary = [];
        foreach (array_chunk($list ?? [], 2) as [$key, $value]) {
            $dictionary[strtolower($key)] = $value;
        }
        return $dictionary;
    }

    // an IMAP disposition ("attachment" (parameters)) or NIL: returns [disposition, parameters]
    private static function disposition(mixed $disposition): array
    {
        if (!is_array($disposition)) {
            return [null, []];
        }
        return [strtolower($disposition[0]), self::dictionary($disposition[1] ?? null)];
    }
}
  • line 7: a class [readonly] (PHP 8.2) has only read-only properties: once constructed, a [MimePart] object can no longer be modified;
  • Lines 9–22: All properties are declared by promoting the constructor’s parameters. They have default values, which allows only certain parameters to be passed by name (named arguments);
  • line 26: the static method [fromBodyStructure] constructs the part tree from the token list in the [BODYSTRUCTURE] response;
  • lines 29–42: A multiple part begins with the lists of its subparts, each of which is converted into a [MimePart] object via a recursive call. Next come its subtype (mixed, alternative, etc.), its parameters (boundary), and its layout;
  • lines 45–57: A simple part begins with its type, subtype, parameters, an identifier, a description, its encoding, and its size. The position of the layout depends on the part’s type: a [text/xxx] part also includes a line count; a [message/rfc822] part also includes the message envelope and structure, as well as a line count. The expression [match (true)] selects the first branch whose condition is true;
  • lines 69–82: the filename of an attachment. We saw in [Mailpit] that it can be encoded in two ways:
    • the encoding RFC 2231 [utf-8''Tah%C3%A9.png]: the character set, two apostrophes, followed by the name encoded as in a URL. It is decoded using [rawurldecode] and then converted to UTF-8 using [mb_convert_encoding];
    • the encoding RFC 2047 [=?utf-8?Q?Tah=C3=A9.png?=]: decode it using the function [iconv_mime_decode];
  • Line 86: A list IMAP [("charset" "utf-8")] becomes the dictionary [["charset" => "utf-8"]];
  • line 96: a layout [("attachment" ("filename" "x.pdf"))] becomes the array [["attachment", ["filename" => "x.pdf"]]].

docs.title: 16.6.6. Client POP3 / IMAP [imap-01.php]
docs.text:
The script [imap-01.php] serves the same purpose as the script of the same name from course PHP 7, which used the functions [imap_open], [imap_num_msg], [imap_search], [imap_headerinfo], [imap_body], [imap_delete], [imap_expunge], and [imap_close]. It uses the following file: JSON [config-imap-01.json]:

{
    "imap.gmail.com:993": {
        "enabled": false,
        "protocol": "imap",
        "server": "imap.gmail.com",
        "port": 993,
        "tls": true,
        "verify-peer": true,
        "user": "php8parlexemple@gmail.com",
        "password": "application password",
        "mailbox": "INBOX",
        "output-dir": "output/gmail-imap"
    },
    "localhost:993": {
        "protocol": "imap",
        "server": "localhost",
        "port": 993,
        "tls": true,
        "verify-peer": false,
        "user": "guest@localhost",
        "password": "guest",
        "mailbox": "INBOX",
        "output-dir": "output/localhost-imap"
    },
    "localhost:1110": {
        "protocol": "pop3",
        "server": "localhost",
        "port": 1110,
        "tls": false,
        "user": "guest",
        "password": "guest",
        "output-dir": "output/localhost-pop3"
    }
}

The file [config-imap-01.json] defines a dictionary of IMAP / POP3 servers to contact. Each entry is in the form [key => value], where:

  • [key]: is a name designating the server. We have three here:
    • [imap.gmail.com:993]: the Gmail server IMAP, which listens on port 993 with an encrypted connection. It is disabled ([enabled] to [false]): enter your Gmail address and app password there, then switch to [enabled] to [true];
    • [localhost:993]: the local IMAP server, with a connection encrypted by a self-signed certificate, which is not verified;
    • [localhost:1110]: the POP3 server of [Mailpit];
  • [value]: is a dictionary specifying the following points:
    • [protocol]: the protocol, [imap] or [pop3];
    • [server]: the server name, IMAP or POP3;
    • [port]: the server port (IMAP or POP3);
    • [tls]: Is the connection encrypted?
    • [verify-peer]: Should the server certificate be verified? On Windows, if the verification fails with a public server, verify that the [openssl.cafile] directive in the [php.ini] file points to a certificate authority file, as does [Laragon];
    • [user]: the mailbox owner;
    • [password]: the mailbox owner’s password;
    • [mailbox]: the IMAP mailbox to be read, with INBOX being the one where new messages arrive;
    • [output-dir]: the folder where messages should be saved.

With the POP3 protocol, after reading a message, it will be deleted. This is how POP3 servers typically operate: a read message is not retained on the server.

The [imap-01.php] script is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) / POP3 client used to read mails
// the mailboxes to read are described in a configuration file

require_once __DIR__ . "/ImapClient.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/Pop3Client.php";

// the parameters for reading the mail
const CONFIG_FILE_NAME = "config-imap-01.json";
// display of the client / server exchanges?
const TRACKING = false;

// we retrieve the configuration
$mailboxes = json_decode(file_get_contents(CONFIG_FILE_NAME), true);

// reading the mailboxes
foreach ($mailboxes as $name => $info) {
    // mailbox disabled in the configuration?
    if (($info["enabled"] ?? true) === false) {
        print "------------Mailbox [$name] disabled\n";
        continue;
    }
    // tracking
    print "------------Reading the mailbox [$name]\n";
    // reading the mailbox
    readmailbox($name, $info);
}
// end
print "Done\n";

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function createClient(array $info): MailClient
{
    // an IMAP or POP3 client depending on the configuration
    return match ($info["protocol"]) {
        "imap" => new ImapClient($info, TRACKING),
        "pop3" => new Pop3Client($info, TRACKING),
    };
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function readmailbox(string $name, array $info): void
{
    // the client of the mailbox
    $client = createClient($info);
    try {
        // connection
        $nbmsg = $client->connect();
        print "Connection established with the server [$name].\n";
        // total of the messages in the mailbox
        print "There are [$nbmsg] messages in the mailbox [$name]\n";
        if ($nbmsg === 0) {
            return;
        }
        // unread messages in the mailbox
        print "Retrieving the list of the unread messages of the mailbox [$name]\n";
        $msgNumbers = $client->unread();
        if (count($msgNumbers) === 0) {
            print "There are no new messages in the mailbox [$name]\n";
            return;
        }
        foreach ($msgNumbers as $msgNumber) {
            // we retrieve the headers of the message no. $msgNumber
            print "Headers of the message no. [$msgNumber] of the mailbox [$name]\n";
            print_r($client->headers($msgNumber));
            // we retrieve the full text of the message no. $msgNumber and save it
            saveMessage($client->message($msgNumber), $msgNumber, $info);
            // if the protocol is POP3, we delete the message
            if ($info["protocol"] === "pop3") {
                $client->delete($msgNumber);
            }
        }
    } catch (RuntimeException $ex) {
        print "Error: " . $ex->getMessage() . "\n";
    } finally {
        // in all cases, we close the connection
        try {
            $client->close();
            print "Connection closed successfully.\n";
        } catch (RuntimeException $ex) {
            print "Closing the connection failed: " . $ex->getMessage() . "\n";
        }
    }
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function saveMessage(string $message, int $msgNumber, array $info): void
{
    // the message is saved in the file [output-dir/message-N.eml]
    $fileName = "{$info["output-dir"]}/message-$msgNumber.eml";
    print "Saving the message in the file [$fileName]\n";
    // we create the folder if need be (true: with its parent folders)
    if (!is_dir($info["output-dir"])) {
        mkdir($info["output-dir"], recursive: true);
    }
    // we save the message
    if (file_put_contents($fileName, $message) === false) {
        print "Saving failed\n";
    }
}

Comments:

  • lines 8–9: the classes for both clients are loaded, which in turn load the [TcpClient] class and the [MailClient] interface;
  • Line 14: In [true], the client/server exchanges are displayed. Give it a try;
  • lines 20–29: We loop through all the servers found in the configuration file, except those that are disabled;
  • lines 35–41: The [createClient] function returns a IMAP or POP3 client, depending on the configuration. Its return type is the [MailClient] interface: the rest of the script does not know which protocol it is dealing with. This is polymorphism;
  • line 51: connection and authentication;
  • line 60: the numbers of unread messages;
  • line 68: the message headers are displayed using the [print_r] function;
  • line 70: the full text of the message is saved to a file;
  • line 72: using the POP3 protocol, the message is marked for deletion;
  • lines 78–86: In all cases, the connection is closed, which deletes the marked messages. If the [return] instructions in the [try] block are executed, the [finally] block is also executed;
  • line 97: the [mkdir] function creates the folder, along with its parent folders, using the argument named [recursive: true].

Let’s run the [smtp-02.php] script so that the user [guest@localhost] has new messages. Once that’s done, let’s run the [imap-01.php] script to read the mailboxes. The console output is as follows:

> php imap-01.php
------------Mailbox [imap.gmail.com:993] disabled
------------Reading the mailbox [localhost:993]
Connection established with the server [localhost:993].
There are [2] messages in the mailbox [localhost:993]
Retrieving the list of the unread messages of the mailbox [localhost:993]
Headers of the message no. [1] of the mailbox [localhost:993]
Array
(
    [From] => guest@localhost
    [To] => guest@localhost
    [Subject] => test-localhost
    [Message-ID] => <b80fff003b5b37b74244dc69674f3ce4@localhost>
    [Date] => Thu, 01 Oct 2026 17:14:39 +0200
    [Flags] =>
    [Size] => 259683
)
Saving the message in the file [output/localhost-imap/message-1.eml]
Headers of the message no. [2] of the mailbox [localhost:993]
Array
(
    [From] => guest@localhost
    [To] => guest@localhost
    [Subject] => test-secure-server
    [Message-ID] => <759bf5367e3f1136ce964ded7f702e09@localhost>
    [Date] => Thu, 01 Oct 2026 17:14:39 +0200
    [Flags] =>
    [Size] => 28101
)
Saving the message in the file [output/localhost-imap/message-2.eml]
Connection closed successfully.
------------Reading the mailbox [localhost:1110]
Connection established with the server [localhost:1110].
There are [2] messages in the mailbox [localhost:1110]
Retrieving the list of the unread messages of the mailbox [localhost:1110]
Headers of the message no. [1] of the mailbox [localhost:1110]
Array
(
    [From] => guest@localhost
    [To] => guest@localhost
    [Subject] => test-secure-server
    [Message-ID] => <759bf5367e3f1136ce964ded7f702e09@localhost>
    [Date] => Thu, 01 Oct 2026 17:14:39 +0200
    [Size] => 28101
)
Saving the message in the file [output/localhost-pop3/message-1.eml]
Headers of the message no. [2] of the mailbox [localhost:1110]
Array
(
    [From] => guest@localhost
    [To] => guest@localhost
    [Subject] => test-localhost
    [Message-ID] => <b80fff003b5b37b74244dc69674f3ce4@localhost>
    [Date] => Thu, 01 Oct 2026 17:14:39 +0200
    [Size] => 259683
)
Saving the message in the file [output/localhost-pop3/message-2.eml]
Connection closed successfully.
Done
  • With IMAP, the two messages deposited in the INBOX mailbox are read. The [Flags] flags are empty: the messages have not yet been read;
  • with POP3, we find the same messages in the [Mailpit] mailbox, in reverse order. The read messages are deleted.

If we then immediately rerun the script [imap-01.php], the results are as follows:

> php imap-01.php
------------Mailbox [imap.gmail.com:993] disabled
------------Reading the mailbox [localhost:993]
Connection established with the server [localhost:993].
There are [2] messages in the mailbox [localhost:993]
Retrieving the list of the unread messages of the mailbox [localhost:993]
There are no new messages in the mailbox [localhost:993]
Connection closed successfully.
------------Reading the mailbox [localhost:1110]
Connection established with the server [localhost:1110].
There are [0] messages in the mailbox [localhost:1110]
Connection closed successfully.
Done
  • There are still the same number of messages in the IMAP mailbox, but there are no longer any unread messages. This shows that the previous execution changed the status of the read messages from “unread” to “read” ([\Seen] flag);
  • There are no more messages in the POP3 inbox: they were deleted during the previous run.

The messages were saved locally in the [output/localhost-imap] and [output/localhost-pop3] folders, under the names [message-1.eml] and [message-2.eml]. The [.eml] file extension is used for email files: double-clicking one of these files opens it in the Windows email client. The file’s contents consist of the complete text of the message, as we saw in the [Raw] tab of [Mailpit]: the message text and the encoded contents of the attachments are mixed together there.

Let’s try to improve this script so that the various parts of the message and the attachments are stored in separate files.

docs.title: 16.6.7. Improved IMAP client ([imap-02.php])
docs.text:
The IMAP server can provide us with a message’s structure (command [BODYSTRUCTURE]) and then the content of each of its parts (command [FETCH n BODY[section]]). We’ll use this in the [imap-02.php] script. The POP3 protocol, on the other hand, only recognizes the entire message: the script will only process the IMAP mailboxes.

Let’s revisit the response to the [BODYSTRUCTURE] command obtained when we discovered the IMAP protocol. It describes a [multipart/mixed]-type message that has six parts:

  • The first part is of type [multipart/alternative]. It itself has two subparts: [text/plain] and [text/html], encoded in [quoted-printable] and having a parameter [charset=utf-8];
  • the next five parts are the attachments, encoded as [base64], each with a layout of [attachment] and a filename.

The parts are numbered as follows:

  • the entire message, of type [multipart/mixed], has no number. Its parts are numbered 1, 2...;
  • when a part has subparts, these are numbered x.1, x.2..., where x is the number of the enclosing part. Thus, the text [text/plain] in the message is part No. 1.1: this is the one we requested with the command [FETCH 2 BODY.PEEK[1.1]].

The script [imap-02.php] is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// IMAP client that saves separately the texts and the attachments of the unread messages
// it uses the MIME structure of the messages provided by the IMAP server (BODYSTRUCTURE command)

require_once __DIR__ . "/ImapClient.php";

// the parameters for reading the mail
const CONFIG_FILE_NAME = "config-imap-01.json";

// we retrieve the configuration
$mailboxes = json_decode(file_get_contents(CONFIG_FILE_NAME), true);

// reading the mailboxes
foreach ($mailboxes as $name => $info) {
    // only the active IMAP mailboxes interest us
    if (($info["enabled"] ?? true) === false || $info["protocol"] !== "imap") {
        continue;
    }
    print "------------Reading the mailbox [$name]\n";
    readmailbox($name, $info);
}
// end
print "Done\n";

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function readmailbox(string $name, array $info): void
{
    $client = new ImapClient($info);
    try {
        // connection
        $nbmsg = $client->connect();
        print "Connection established with the server [$name].\n";
        print "There are [$nbmsg] messages in the mailbox [$name]\n";
        // unread messages
        print "Retrieving the list of the unread messages of the mailbox [$name]\n";
        $msgNumbers = $client->unread();
        if (count($msgNumbers) === 0) {
            print "There are no new messages in the mailbox [$name]\n";
        }
        foreach ($msgNumbers as $msgNumber) {
            // the headers of the message will be used to prefix its texts
            $headers = $client->headers($msgNumber);
            // the structure of the message
            $structure = $client->structure($msgNumber);
            // we go through its parts
            $outputDir = "{$info["output-dir"]}/message-$msgNumber";
            getParts($client, $msgNumber, $structure, "", $outputDir, $headers);
        }
    } catch (RuntimeException $ex) {
        print "Error: " . $ex->getMessage() . "\n";
    } finally {
        try {
            $client->close();
            print "Connection closed successfully.\n";
        } catch (RuntimeException $ex) {
            print "Closing the connection failed: " . $ex->getMessage() . "\n";
        }
    }
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function getParts(ImapClient $client, int $msgNumber, MimePart $part, string $section,
    string $outputDir, array $headers): void
{
    // displays the type of the part [$part] of the message no. $msgNumber, then:
    // - if it has subparts, processes them in turn (recursive call);
    // - otherwise, saves it in the folder [$outputDir]
    // $section is the IMAP number of the part: 1, 2, 1.1, 1.2...
    // the root part (the whole message) has no number: we display 0
    print "-----content of the part no. [" . ($section === "" ? "0" : $section) . "]\n";
    print "Content-Type: " . strtoupper("$part->type/$part->subType") . "\n";
    print "Transfer-Encoding: $part->encoding\n";
    // subparts?
    if ($part->type === "multipart") {
        foreach ($part->parts as $i => $subpart) {
            // the subparts of the part no. x are numbered x.1, x.2...
            $subsection = $section === "" ? (string) ($i + 1) : "$section." . ($i + 1);
            getParts($client, $msgNumber, $subpart, $subsection, $outputDir, $headers);
        }
        return;
    }
    // a message that is not multipart has a single part, numbered 1
    if ($section === "") {
        $section = "1";
    }
    // we save the part
    savePart($client, $msgNumber, $part, $section, $outputDir, $headers);
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function savePart(ImapClient $client, int $msgNumber, MimePart $part, string $section,
    string $outputDir, array $headers): void
{
    // if the folder does not exist, we create it
    if (!is_dir($outputDir)) {
        mkdir($outputDir, recursive: true);
    }
    // an attachment?
    $fileName = $part->fileName();
    if ($part->disposition === "attachment" && $fileName !== null) {
        saveAttachment($client->part($msgNumber, $section), $part, "$outputDir/$fileName");
        return;
    }
    // a text?
    match ("$part->type/$part->subType") {
        "text/plain" => saveText("$outputDir/message.txt", false,
            $client->part($msgNumber, $section), $part, $headers),
        "text/html" => saveText("$outputDir/message.html", true,
            $client->part($msgNumber, $section), $part, $headers),
        // other cases: this part will not be processed
        default => print "Part [$section] ignored\n",
    };
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function decode(string $text, string $encoding): string
{
    // decoding of a content encoded in base64 or in quoted-printable
    return match ($encoding) {
        "base64" => base64_decode($text),
        "quoted-printable" => quoted_printable_decode($text),
        // 7bit, 8bit, binary: no encoding
        default => $text,
    };
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function saveText(string $fileName, bool $html, string $text, MimePart $part, array $headers): void
{
    // the text is decoded then converted to UTF-8 if it uses another character set
    $text = decode($text, $part->encoding);
    $charset = $part->parameters["charset"] ?? "utf-8";
    if (strtolower($charset) !== "utf-8") {
        $text = mb_convert_encoding($text, "UTF-8", $charset);
    }
    // we precede it with the From, To, Subject headers of the message
    $endOfLine = $html ? "<br/>\n" : "\n";
    $content = "From: {$headers["From"]}$endOfLine"
        . "To: {$headers["To"]}$endOfLine"
        . "Subject: {$headers["Subject"]}$endOfLine$endOfLine"
        . $text;
    print "Saving a message in [$fileName]\n";
    if (file_put_contents($fileName, $content) === false) {
        print "Unable to create the file [$fileName]\n";
    }
}

// --------------------------------------------------------------------------
function saveAttachment(string $content, MimePart $part, string $fileName): void
{
    print "Saving the attachment in [$fileName]\n";
    if (file_put_contents($fileName, decode($content, $part->encoding)) === false) {
        print "The attachment could not be saved in [$fileName]\n";
    }
}

Comments:

  • line 19: only active IMAP mailboxes are read;
  • line 45: the message headers will be used to prefix the stored text;
  • line 47: the message structure: a [MimePart] object;
  • line 50: the [getParts] function iterates through the message parts. It starts with the root part—the entire message—which has no section number;
  • line 65: the function [getParts] receives the following parameters:
    • [$client]: the client IMAP;
    • [$msgNumber]: the message number for which the parts are requested;
    • [$part]: an object representing a part of the message;
    • [$section]: the number of that part;
    • [$outputDir]: the folder where the parts should be saved;
    • [$headers]: general information about the email (sender, recipient, subject, etc.);
  • lines 73–75: the part number, content type, and encoding are displayed. The entire message is displayed as part number 0;
  • lines 77–83: if the part has subparts, each one is retrieved via a recursive call to the function [getParts]. Their section number is [$section.i];
  • lines 86–87: A message that is not multipart (plain text) has only one part, numbered 1;
  • line 90: when there are no subparts, the content of the part is stored;
  • line 94: the function [savePart] records a part:
    • if it is an attachment (setting [attachment]), it is saved using the function [saveAttachment] under its file name;
    • If the text is [text/plain] or [text/html], it is saved using the [saveText] function to the file [message.txt] or [message.html]. The other parts are ignored;
    • in both cases, the content of the section is requested from the IMAP server using the client’s [part] method;
  • line 119: the content of a section is encoded. The functions [base64_decode] and [quoted_printable_decode] decode it;
  • line 131: The text is decoded, then converted to UTF-8 using the [mb_convert_encoding] function if it uses a different character set (parameter [charset]). It is preceded by the message headers [From], [To], and [Subject]. In the case of HTML text, each header is followed by a [<br/>] tag so that it appears on its own line in a browser;
  • line 152: an attachment is decoded and then saved.

To test the script [imap-02.php], first send an email to [guest@localhost] with the script [smtp-02.php] (the message [test-localhost] and its five attachments), which is deposited in the INBOX mailbox on the IMAP server. It is then read using [imap-02.php]. The console output is as follows:

The message structure is correctly preserved. The files were saved in the [output/localhost-imap/message-3] folder:
