{"action":"list-simulations","status":103,"response":["no session in progress. Start with action [init-session]"]}
  • Lines 1–2: A request without the [action] parameter in URL: status [101];
  • lines 4–5: a request with an invalid [action] parameter: status [102];
  • lines 7–8: an action recognized but the session type (json, xml, html) has not yet been specified: status [103].

In all three cases, the key [response] is an error list, in this instance containing a single error.

docs.title: 23.10. Secondary controllers
docs.text:
Each action is executed by one of the controllers in the [Controllers] folder:

In the overall architecture of the application above, the secondary controllers are in [2a]. Each controller implements the following [InterfaceController] interface:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// the interface implemented by all the secondary controllers
interface InterfaceController
{
    // processing of the requested action
    // array $config: the application's configuration
    // Request $request: the request being processed
    // Session $session: the web application's session, which the controller may modify
    // returns a [ControllerResult] object: HTTP status, application status, response, HTTP headers
    public function execute(array $config, Request $request, Session $session): ControllerResult;
}

Comments

  • Line 20: All secondary controllers are executed via the [execute] method. Information known to the main controller is passed to this method:
    • [array $config]: the application configuration;
    • [Request $request]: the HTTP request currently being processed;
    • [Session $session]: the current web application session;
  • The [execute] method returns a [ControllerResult] object: the response status code HTTP, the state of the application at the end of execution, the response to be sent to the client, and the headers HTTP to be added to the response.

Method PHP 7 had a fourth parameter, [array $infos = NULL], which was included “just in case” but never used: we have removed it. Each secondary controller is called by the following code in the main controller:

    // we execute the action with its secondary controller
    $controller = match ($action) {
        Action::InitSession => new InitSessionController(),
        Action::AuthenticateUser => new AuthenticateUserController(),
        Action::CalculateTax => new CalculateTaxController(),
        Action::ListSimulations => new ListSimulationsController(),
        Action::DeleteSimulation => new DeleteSimulationController(),
        Action::EndSession => new EndSessionController(),
        Action::DisplayTaxCalculation => new DisplayTaxCalculationController(),
    };
    $logger->write("controller : " . $controller::class);
    $result = $controller->execute($config, $request, $session);

docs.title: 23.11. Actions
docs.text:
We will now review the various possible actions of the web service:

ActionRoleExecution Contextinit-sessionUsed to specify the type (json, xml, html) of the desired responsesRequest GET main.php?action=init-session&type=xCan be issued at any timeauthenticate-userAuthorizes or denies a user’s loginRequest POST main.php?action=authenticate-userThe request must include two POST parameters: [user, password]Can only be issued if the session type (json, xml, html) is knowncalculate-taxPerforms a tax calculation simulationRequest: POST main.php?action=calculate-taxThe request must have three POST parameters: [married, children, salary]Can only be issued if the session type is known and the user is authenticatedlist-simulationsRequests a list of simulations performed since the start of the sessionRequest GET main.php?action=list-simulationsThe request does not accept any other parametersCan only be issued if the session type is known and the user is authenticateddelete-simulationDeletes a simulation from the list of simulationsRequest GET main.php?action=delete-simulation&number=xThe request does not accept any other parametersCan only be issued if the session type is known and the user is authenticatedend-sessionEnds the simulation sessionRequest GET main.php?action=end-sessionTechnically, the old web session is deleted and a new session is createdCan only be issued if the session type is known and the user is authenticateddisplay-tax-calculationDisplays the tax calculation view (application HTML)Request GET main.php?action=display-tax-calculationCan only be issued if the session type is known and the user is authenticated

All secondary controllers proceed in the same way:

  • they check their parameters. These are found in the [$request->query] object for parameters present in the URL object and in the [$request->request] object for those that are posted (request POST);
  • A controller is similar to a function or method that checks the validity of its parameters. For the controller, however, it’s a bit more complicated:
    • the expected parameters may be missing;
    • the expected parameters are all character strings, whereas a function can specify the type of its parameters. If the expected parameter is a number, then you must verify that the parameter’s string actually represents a number;
    • once it has been verified that the expected parameters are present and syntactically correct, you must verify that they are valid within the current execution context. This context is stored in the session. Authentication is an example of an execution context: certain actions should only be processed once the client has been authenticated. A key in the session indicates whether this authentication has taken place or not;
  • Once the previous checks have been completed, the secondary controller can begin processing. This parameter validation is very important. We cannot allow a client to send us just anything at any point during the application’s lifecycle. We must maintain complete control over the application’s lifecycle;
  • Once its work is done, the secondary controller returns the [ControllerResult] object expected by the primary controller that called it.

We will now review the various controllers—or, in other words, the various actions that drive the web application’s lifecycle.

docs.title: 23.11.1. The [init-session] action
docs.text:
The action [init-session] is handled by the following controller, [InitSessionController]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// action [init-session]: sets the type (json, xml, html) of the session's responses
final class InitSessionController implements InterfaceController
{
    #[\Override]
    public function execute(array $config, Request $request, Session $session): ControllerResult
    {
        // we must have a GET with only the parameters [action, type] in the URL
        if ($request->getMethod() !== "GET" || $request->query->count() !== 2) {
            $message = "GET method required with parameters [action, type] in the URL";
            return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, 701, $message);
        }
        // the [type] parameter must be present
        if (!$request->query->has("type")) {
            return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, 702, "missing parameter [type]");
        }
        // and valid: [tryFrom] returns null if the string is not the value of any case of the enumeration
        $type = strtolower(trim($request->query->getString("type")));
        if (ResponseType::tryFrom($type) === null) {
            return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, 703, "invalid type parameter [$type]");
        }
        // we put the session type in the session
        $session->set("type", $type);
        // success
        return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_OK, 700, "session started with type [$type]");
    }
}

Comments

  • A request for [GET main.php?action=init-session&type=xxx] is expected;
  • Line 14: The class implements the [InterfaceController] interface. It is [final]: it cannot be derived from;
  • Lines 20–23: We verify that the request is a GET request with two parameters in the URL. If this is not the case, an error result is returned to the main controller with the status [701]. The Symfony method [getMethod] returns the name of the method HTTP in uppercase: it is no longer necessary to convert it to lowercase as the script PHP 7 did;
  • lines 25–27: We verify that the parameter [type] is present in URL. If not, we return an error result with status [702];
  • line 29: Record the session type;
  • Lines 30–32: Check that the session type is one of the terms (json, xml, html), i.e. the value must be one of the cases in the enumeration [ResponseType]. If this is not the case, return an error result with status [703];
  • line 34: the session type is set in the web application session;
  • line 36: the controller has finished its work. A success result is returned to the main controller, with status [700].

Every error case results in an immediate [return]. The script PHP 7 used a Boolean variable [$error] that was checked at each step: the code is now shorter and more readable. Let’s review what the main controller does with the responses from the secondary controllers: it adds the keys [action] and [status] to the response and sends it by instantiating one of the [JsonResponse, XmlResponse, HtmlResponse] classes depending on the type (json, xml, html) of the current session.

Next, we will perform [curl] tests as part of a [json] simulation session.

{"action":"init-session","status":700,"response":"session started with type [json]"}
  • Lines 1–2: the [init-session] action without the [type] parameter: the request does not have the two expected parameters; status [701];
  • lines 4–5: the action [init-session] with parameter [typ] instead of [type]: status [702];
  • lines 7–8: action [init-session] with an incorrect parameter [type]: status [703];
  • lines 10–20: action [init-session] with type [json]: status [700].

The [-c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt] options cause [curl] to handle the session cookie like a browser. The cookie was sent by the server in its response to the first request (lines 1–2); [curl] saved it to the file [cookies.txt] and sends it back with every request. The server no longer sends it (lines 11–18); it only does so at the start of a new session. The file [cookies.txt] now contains:

# Netscape HTTP Cookie File

docs.title: 23.11.3. The [authenticate-user] action
docs.text:
The action [authenticate-user] is executed by the following controller, [AuthenticateUserController]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// action [authenticate-user]: authenticates the user with the posted parameters [user, password]
final class AuthenticateUserController implements InterfaceController
{
    #[\Override]
    public function execute(array $config, Request $request, Session $session): ControllerResult
    {
        // we must have a POST with the single parameter [action] in the URL
        if ($request->getMethod() !== "POST" || $request->query->count() !== 1) {
            $message = "POST method required, parameter [action] in the URL, posted parameters [user, password]";
            return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, 201, $message);
        }
        // we retrieve the posted parameters
        $errors = [];
        $status = 210;
        // user
        if (!$request->request->has("user")) {
            $status += 2;
            $errors[] = "missing parameter [user]";
        }
        // password
        if (!$request->request->has("password")) {
            $status += 4;
            $errors[] = "missing parameter [password]";
        }
        // errors?
        if ($errors !== []) {
            return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, $status, $errors);
        }
        $user = trim($request->request->getString("user"));
        $password = trim($request->request->getString("password"));
        // is the user one of the authorized users?
        $found = array_any(
            $config["users"],
            fn(array $u): bool => $u["login"] === $user && hash_equals($u["passwd"], $password)
        );
        if (!$found) {
            // failure: code 401 - the password is never sent back to the client
            return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_UNAUTHORIZED, 221, "Authentication failed [$user]");
        }
        // we note in the session the identifier of the authenticated user
        $session->set("user", $user);
        // success
        return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_OK, 200, "Authentication successful [$user]");
    }
}

Comments

  • We are waiting for a [POST main.php?action=authenticate-user] request with two posted parameters, [user, password];
  • Lines 20–23: The system checks whether there is a POST request with a single parameter in URL. If not, an error result is returned with status [201];
  • line 26: the error status for the posted parameters starts at value 210;
  • lines 28–31: We check for the presence of the parameter [user] in the posted values. If it is not present, we log the error and increment the status by 2;
  • Lines 33–36: We check for the presence of the parameter [password]. If it is not present, we log the error and add 4 to the status. The status is therefore 212 if only [user] is missing, 214 if only [password] is missing, and 216 if both are missing;
  • lines 38–40: if any of the posted values is missing, an error result is returned, with the response being the list of errors;
  • lines 41–42: the posted identifiers;
  • lines 44–47: verify that the pair [[$user, $password]] is present in the [$config["users"]] array in the configuration file. The function [array_any] (PHP 8.4) returns [true] if at least one element of the array satisfies the condition expressed by the arrowed function. The password is compared using the function [hash_equals], whose execution time does not depend on the position of the first differing character: an attacker cannot guess the password character by character by measuring response times. The script PHP 7 used a loop [while];
  • lines 48–51: if the user is not found, an error result is returned with status HTTP [401 Unauthorized] and status [221]. Message PHP 7 contained the entered password: a password must never be sent back to the client or written to the logs;
  • line 53: authentication was successful. This is recorded in the session by adding the key [user], with the user ID as its value. The presence of this key indicates successful authentication;
  • Line 55: A success result is returned to the main controller, with the status [200].

docs.title: 23.11.5. Action [calculate-tax]
docs.text:
The [calculate-tax] action is processed by the following [CalculateTaxController] controller:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;
// Predis dependencies
use Predis\Client as RedisClient;
use Predis\PredisException;
// class alias: the [dao] layer of version 9 is used with Redis
use Application\ServerDaoWithSession as ServerDaoWithRedis;

// action [calculate-tax]: tax calculation with the posted parameters [married, children, salary]
final class CalculateTaxController implements InterfaceController
{
    #[\Override]
    public function execute(array $config, Request $request, Session $session): ControllerResult
    {
        // we must have a POST with the single parameter [action] in the URL
        if ($request->getMethod() !== "POST" || $request->query->count() !== 1) {
            $message = "you must use the [post] method with [action] in the URL"
                . " and the posted parameters [married, children, salary]";
            return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, 301, $message);
        }
        // we check the posted parameters
        // each error adds a different value to the status: the final status tells which errors occurred
        $errors = [];
        $status = 310;
        // marital status
        if (!$request->request->has("married")) {
            $status += 2;
            $errors[] = "missing parameter [married]";
        } else {
            $married = strtolower(trim($request->request->getString("married")));
            if (!in_array($married, ["yes", "no"], true)) {
                $status += 4;
                $errors[] = "invalid value [$married] for parameter [married]";
            }
        }
        // number of children and annual salary: integers >= 0
        $values = [];
        foreach (["children" => [8, 9], "salary" => [16, 17]] as $parameter => [$missing, $invalid]) {
            if (!$request->request->has($parameter)) {
                $status += $missing;
                $errors[] = "missing parameter [$parameter]";
                continue;
            }
            $value = trim($request->request->getString($parameter));
            if (preg_match('/^\d+$/', $value) !== 1) {
                $status += $invalid;
                $errors[] = "invalid value [$value] for parameter [$parameter]";
            } else {
                $values[$parameter] = (int) $value;
            }
        }
        // errors?
        if ($errors !== []) {
            return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, $status, $errors);
        }
        [$children, $salary] = [$values["children"], $values["salary"]];

        // we have valid parameters - the [application]-scope memory: a Redis server
        try {
            $redis = new RedisClient($config["redis"]);
            // we connect to the server right away to find out whether it is there
            $redis->connect();
        } catch (PredisException $ex) {
            // error 500
            return new ControllerResult(
                Response::HTTP_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
                350,
                "[redis], " . self::utf8($ex->getMessage())
            );
        }
        // creating the [dao] layer
        try {
            $json = $redis->get("taxAdminData");
            if ($json === null) {
                // the tax data are taken from the database then put in Redis
                $dao = new ServerDaoWithRedis(ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["databaseFilename"]);
                $redis->set("taxAdminData", (string) $dao->getTaxAdminData());
            } else {
                // the tax data are taken from Redis
                $taxAdminData = TaxAdminData::fromArray(json_decode($json, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR));
                $dao = new ServerDaoWithRedis($taxAdminData);
            }
        } catch (TaxException $ex) {
            // error 500
            return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, 341, self::utf8($ex->getMessage()));
        } finally {
            // we no longer need the Redis server
            $redis->disconnect();
        }
        // creating the [business] layer and calculating the tax
        $result = (new ServerBusiness($dao))->calculateTax($married, $children, $salary);
        // the simulation: the keys of the [$result] array become named arguments
        $simulation = new Simulation($married, $children, $salary, ...$result);
        // we add it to the session's list of simulations
        $session->set("simulations", [...$session->get("simulations", []), $simulation]);
        // success
        return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_OK, 300, $simulation);
    }

    // the error message of a DBMS or Redis driver may not be UTF-8 encoded
    // (Windows-1252 on Windows): it could then not be put in a JSON string
    private static function utf8(string $message): string
    {
        return mb_check_encoding($message, "UTF-8") ? $message : mb_convert_encoding($message, "UTF-8", "Windows-1252");
    }
}

Comments

  • The expected request is [POST main.php?action=calculate-tax] with three posted parameters [married, children, salary]:
    • [married] must have its value in [yes, no];
    • [children, salary] must be positive integers or zero;
  • Lines 13–16: As in version 10, we use the [Predis] library and the [dao] layer from version 9, under the alias [ServerDaoWithRedis];
  • lines 25–29: We verify that there is indeed a POST with a single parameter in the URL. If this is not the case, an error result is returned to the main controller, with status [301];
  • lines 32–33: error messages are accumulated in the array [$errors]. The count starts at 310, and each error increments it by one;
  • lines 35–44: We check for the presence of parameter [married] (+2 if missing), then verify that its value is in [yes, no] (+4 otherwise);
  • lines 47–60: The parameters [children] and [salary] are checked by the same loop. The array being iterated through associates each parameter with the pair of values added to the state when the parameter is missing or invalid: (8, 9) for [children], (16, 17) for [salary]. The unpacking of [[$missing, $invalid]] is performed directly within the [foreach] statement. The PHP script 7 wrote the same code twice;
    • lines 48–52: the parameter is missing; the [continue] statement moves on to the next parameter;
    • lines 54–59: the value must be a sequence of at least one digit. If so, it is converted to an integer and stored in the array [$values];
  • lines 62–64: If there were any errors, a result is returned containing a list of the errors;
  • line 65: the parameters are valid. The tax can be calculated. To do this, the layers [dao] and [business] must be created, which are capable of performing this calculation;
  • lines 68–79: A client named [Redis] is created, and a connection to the server is established immediately. If we were unable to connect to the server [Redis], we return a result with status [500 Internal Server Error] and condition [350];
  • lines 81–98: construction of the [dao] layer:
    • Line 82: Check whether the server [Redis] has the key [taxAdminData]. This key represents the tax administration data. The method [get] of [Predis] returns [null] if the key does not exist;
    • line 85: the key does not exist; the tax data must be retrieved from the database. The path to the database description file is relative to the application’s root directory, which is determined by the constant [ROOT_DIRECTORY] defined by [main.php];
    • line 86: the data retrieved from the database is stored in memory [Redis] with the key [taxAdminData], in the form of its string JSON;
    • lines 89–90: if the key [taxAdminData] exists in memory [Redis], the tax data is passed directly to the layer builder [dao];
  • lines 92–94: if the database query failed, a result is returned with status [500 Internal Server Error], application status [341], and the exception message thrown by layer [dao]. The listing for course PHP 7 showed status 340 here, whereas its source code, its configuration (which associates status 341 with the tax calculation view), and its text all used 341. We chose 341: status 340 is already the status for a request with three invalid posted parameters (310 + 4 + 9 + 17);
  • lines 95–98: the [finally] clause is executed in all cases, regardless of whether an exception occurred, and even if the [catch] block ends with a [return]. Here, the connection to the [Redis] server is closed;
  • line 100: the [business] layer is created and calculates the tax. The result is the [tax, surcharge, discount, reduction, rate] array;
  • Line 102: Based on the result of the calculation, an object [Simulation] is created. The first three arguments are positional. The operator [...] then decomposes the associative array [$result]: Starting with PHP 8.1, its keys become named arguments—in this case, [tax, surcharge, discount, reduction, rate]—which are the names of the last parameters of the constructor;
  • line 104: the simulation that has just been constructed is added to the list of simulations already calculated, which is located in the session. The second parameter of the session’s [get] method is the value returned if the key is absent: an empty list if no simulations have been performed yet. The new list is constructed by decomposing the old list, followed by the new simulation, and then returned to the session;
  • line 106: the simulation is returned to the main controller, with the status [300];
  • line 111: An error message from a DBMS driver may not be encoded as UTF-8 (see version 8). In that case, it could not be placed in a JSON string. The PHP 7 script used the [utf8_encode] function, which has been deprecated since PHP 8.2; we now use [mb_convert_encoding].

docs.text:
We are testing the [CalculateTaxController] controller in JSON mode, with the user authenticated:

{"action":"calculate-tax","status":340,"response":["invalid value [maybe] for parameter [married]","invalid value [x] for parameter [children]","invalid value [y] for parameter [salary]"]}

> curl -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/main.php?action=calculate-tax" -d "salary=y"
{"action":"calculate-tax","status":337,"response":["missing parameter [married]","missing parameter [children]","invalid value [y] for parameter [salary]"]}

> curl -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/main.php?action=calculate-tax" --data-urlencode "married=yes" -d "children=2&salary=55555"
{"action":"calculate-tax","status":300,"response":{"married":"yes","children":2,"salary":55555,"tax":2814,"surcharge":0,"discount":0,"reduction":0,"rate":0.14}}

> curl -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/main.php?action=calculate-tax" --data-urlencode "married=no" -d "children=3&salary=200000"
{"action":"calculate-tax","status":300,"response":{"married":"no","children":3,"salary":200000,"tax":58006,"surcharge":26649,"discount":0,"reduction":0,"rate":0.45}}
  • Lines 1–2: We make a request for GET instead of POST: status [301];
  • lines 4–5: a request POST with all three parameters from [married, children, salary] present and all invalid: status 310 + 4 + 9 + 17 = 340;
  • lines 7–8: only the parameter [salary] is posted, and it is also invalid: status 310 + 2 + 8 + 17 = 337;
  • lines 10–11: a tax calculation with valid parameters: record [300]. The result is the JSON object from the simulation. This matches the tax amount of 2,814 euros from the official 2019 example for a couple with two children and an income of 55,555 euros;
  • Lines 13–14: a second tax calculation.

Note that the status does not always indicate a unique combination of errors: 8 + 17 = 9 + 16. Status 337 also corresponds to a request where [married] and [salary] are missing and where [children] is invalid. The list of error messages provides a precise description of the errors.

Server: Apache/2.4.58
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Cache-Control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate
Cache-Control: no-cache, private
Connection: close
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"action":"calculate-tax","status":350,"response":"[redis], Connection refused [tcp://127.0.0.1:6380]"}

  • line 14: the status [350] and the exception message thrown by [Predis].

An email was sent to the application administrator: this can be seen in the web interface for [Mailpit] (URL [http://localhost:8025]). Its subject line is [tax calculation server crash], and its body contains the response JSON sent to the client. Don’t forget to restore port 6379.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// action [list-simulations]: returns the list of the session's simulations
final class ListSimulationsController implements InterfaceController
{
    #[\Override]
    public function execute(array $config, Request $request, Session $session): ControllerResult
    {
        // we must have a GET with the single parameter [action] in the URL
        if ($request->getMethod() !== "GET" || $request->query->count() !== 1) {

Comments

docs.title: 23.11.9. Action [delete-simulation]
docs.text:
Action [delete-simulation] is processed by the following secondary controller, [DeleteSimulationController]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// action [delete-simulation]: deletes simulation no. [number] from the list of simulations
final class DeleteSimulationController implements InterfaceController
{
    #[\Override]
    public function execute(array $config, Request $request, Session $session): ControllerResult
    {
        // we must have a GET with only the parameters [action, number] in the URL
        if ($request->getMethod() !== "GET" || $request->query->count() !== 2) {
            return self::error(602, "GET required, with the parameters [action, number]");
        }
        // the [number] parameter must exist
        if (!$request->query->has("number")) {
            return self::error(604, "missing parameter [number]");
        }
        // the [number] parameter must be an integer >= 0
        $number = trim($request->query->getString("number"));
        if (preg_match('/^\d+$/', $number) !== 1) {
            return self::error(612, "invalid parameter [$number]");
        }
        // simulation no. [number] must exist: [number] in the interval [0, n-1]
        $number = (int) $number;
        $simulations = $session->get("simulations", []);
        if ($number >= count($simulations)) {
            return self::error(628, "simulation no. [$number] does not exist");
        }
        // we delete the simulation: [array_splice] renumbers the following elements of the list
        array_splice($simulations, $number, 1);
        // we put the simulations back in the session
        $session->set("simulations", $simulations);
        // we return the new list of simulations
        return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_OK, 600, $simulations);
    }

    // an error result
    private static function error(int $status, string $message): ControllerResult
    {
        return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, $status, $message);
    }
}

Comments

  • request [GET main.php?action=delete-simulation&number=x];
  • lines 20–22: Check that there is a request GET with two parameters. Otherwise, the status is [602];
  • lines 24–26: Check that the parameter [number] exists among the parameters of URL. Otherwise, the status is [604];
  • lines 28–31: Check that the value of parameter [number] is syntactically correct: a positive integer or zero. Otherwise, the status is [612];
  • lines 33–37: Verify that simulation No. [number] actually exists: the number must be in the range [0, n-1], where n is the number of simulations in the session. Otherwise, the status is [628]. Since the number cannot be negative, it is sufficient to verify that it is less than n. If the session contains no simulations, n is 0;
  • line 39: simulation No. [number] is deleted by function [array_splice], which deletes an element starting at position [$number] and renumbers the subsequent elements. The script PHP 7 used [unset], which does not change the keys of the other elements, and then [array_values] to obtain a list with keys [0, n-2];
  • line 41: the new simulation table is returned to the session;
  • line 43: the new list of simulations is returned to the main controller, with the status [600];
  • line 47: a utility method that constructs an error result. The error statuses are those from script PHP 7, which calculated them by adding 2, 4, 8, and then 16 to status 600 as the checks progressed.

docs.title: 23.11.11. Action [end-session]
docs.text:
Action [end-session] is processed by the following secondary controller, [EndSessionController]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// action [end-session]: ends the simulation session
final class EndSessionController implements InterfaceController
{
    #[\Override]
    public function execute(array $config, Request $request, Session $session): ControllerResult
    {
        // we must have a GET with the single parameter [action] in the URL
        if ($request->getMethod() !== "GET" || $request->query->count() !== 1) {
            $message = "GET required with the single parameter [action] in the URL";
            return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST, 401, $message);
        }
        // we store the session type
        $type = $session->get("type");
        // we invalidate the current session: its data are deleted and a new session starts
        $session->invalidate();
        // we put the type back in the new session
        $session->set("type", $type);
        // success
        return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_OK, 400, "session deleted");
    }
}

Comments

  • request [GET main.php?action=end-session];
  • lines 20–23: Verify that the action is a GET with the single parameter [action]. Otherwise, the status is [401];
  • line 25: Before the session ends, the session type ([json, xml, html]) is stored;
  • line 27: the current session is invalidated. This deletes the data stored in it, and a new session is started with a new identifier;
  • Line 29: The type from the previous session is restored in the new session. Finally, we start over with a new session having the unique key [type]: the user will need to authenticate again;
  • Line 31: The result is returned to the main controller, with the status [400].

Cache-Control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate
Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=deleted; expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:01 GMT; Max-Age=0; path=/

  • Lines 1–2: We request session termination with a POST instead of the expected GET: status [401];
  • Lines 4–16: A valid [end-session] action: status [400];
  • lines 10–11: the server sends two [Set-Cookie] headers. The first instructs the client to delete the old session cookie (its expiration date has passed). The second provides the client with the new session cookie: a new web session begins. We saw that, within the same session, the server no longer sends the session cookie after the first response;
  • lines 18–19: In the new session, the user is no longer authenticated: status [104].

docs.title: 23.12.1. Introduction
docs.text:
Let’s review the application’s overall architecture:

We will now present the possible response types [3a]. These are located in the [Responses] folder of the project. We have already introduced the [InterfaceResponse] interface, the parent class [ParentResponse], and the [JsonResponse] class. The response type for a session is set by the action [init-session], which places it in the session. It is represented by the enumeration [ResponseType] in the folder [Entities]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the response types the client can request with the [init-session] action
enum ResponseType: string
{
    case Json = "json";
    case Xml = "xml";
    case Html = "html";

    // the object responsible for sending a response of this type
    public function response(): InterfaceResponse
    {
        return match ($this) {
            self::Json => new JsonResponse(),
            self::Xml => new XmlResponse(),
            self::Html => new HtmlResponse(),
        };
    }
}

Comments

  • lines 11–13: the three response types. The value for each case is the expected value for the [type] parameter of action [init-session];
  • Lines 16–23: The [response] method returns the object responsible for sending a response of this type. The return type is the [InterfaceResponse] interface: the calling code is only aware of the [send] method of the interface. The PHP 7 course associated each type in the configuration file with a class name (key [types]) and instantiated it using [new $response()].

Let’s review the code from the main controller that requests that the response be sent to the client:

// the type of the response is in the session - JSON by default if it has not been set yet
$type = ResponseType::tryFrom($session->get("type", "")) ?? ResponseType::Json;
// the [InterfaceResponse] object of the requested type sends the response to the client
$type->response()->send(
    $request,
    $session,
    $config,
    $result->statusCode,
    $content,
    $result->headers,
    $logger
);
  • Line 107: The response type is determined;
  • line 109: the appropriate response class is instantiated, and the response is sent to the client using its method [send($request, $session, $config, $statusCode, $content, $headers, $logger)].

docs.title: 23.12.2. The [JsonResponse] class
docs.text:
has already been introduced. However, we are including its code again to better highlight the consistency among the three response classes:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// a JSON response
final class JsonResponse extends ParentResponse
{
    #[\Override]
    public function send(
        Request $request,
        Session $session,
        array $config,
        int $statusCode,
        array $content,
        array $headers = [],
        ?Logger $logger = null
    ): void {
        // JSON serialization: [json_encode] also serializes the public attributes of the [Simulation] objects
        $json = json_encode($content, self::JSON_OPTIONS);
        // sending the response by the parent class
        $this->sendResponse($statusCode, $json, "application/json", $headers);
        // log
        $logger?->write("response=$json");
    }
}

docs.title: 23.12.3. The [XmlResponse] class
docs.text:
The [XmlResponse] class is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// an XML response
final class XmlResponse extends ParentResponse
{
    #[\Override]
    public function send(
        Request $request,
        Session $session,
        array $config,
        int $statusCode,
        array $content,
        array $headers = [],
        ?Logger $logger = null
    ): void {
        // XML serialization with the [XmlUtilities] class of version 11
        // the [Simulation] objects are first turned into associative arrays
        $xml = XmlUtilities::arrayToXml(self::toArray($content), "root");
        // sending the response by the parent class
        $this->sendResponse($statusCode, $xml, "application/xml", $headers);
        // log in JSON, more concise than XML
        $this->log($logger, $content);
    }
}

Comments

  • Line 27: The response [$content] is serialized to XML by the method [arrayToXml] of the class [XmlUtilities] in version 11. This method expects an array whose values are either arrays or simple values: the [toArray] method of the parent class first replaces the [Simulation] objects with the array of their attributes. The root element of the document is named [root], as in course PHP 7;
  • line 29: the parent class sends the response to the client, with the type [application/xml];
  • line 31: the response is logged as JSON, which is more concise than XML.

The PHP 7 course used the XML encoder from the [Symfony / Serializer] library, and a second encoder, JSON, for the logs.

docs.title: 23.12.4. [curl] Tests
docs.text:

  • lines 9–15: a successful authentication;
  • lines 17–32: a tax calculation. The element [response] contains the simulation attributes as child elements;

docs.title: 23.12.5. The [HtmlResponse] response
docs.text:
When the session type is [html], an object of type [HtmlResponse] is instantiated to send the response to the client. This object will send the client a HTML document, which depends on the status code returned by the secondary controller that processed the action. This mapping, [status => view], is entered in the configuration file [config.json] as follows:

    "views": {
        "view-authentication.php": [700, 221, 400],
        "view-tax-calculation.php": [200, 300, 341, 350, 800],
        "view-simulations-list.php": [500, 600]
    },
    "view-errors": "view-errors.php"

This configuration is interpreted as follows: [‘view name' => ‘statuses associated with this view']:

  • line 56: if the secondary controller returned a status from the [700, 221, 400] array, then display the [view-authentication.php] view;
  • line 57: if the secondary controller returned a status from the [200, 300, 341, 350, 800] array, then display the [view-tax-calculation.php] view;
  • Line 58: If the secondary controller returned a status from the [500, 600] array, then display the [view-simulations-list.php] view;
  • Line 60: If the secondary controller has returned a status that is not in any of the previous arrays, then display view [view-errors.php].

The views are contained in the [Views] folder of the project. The code for the [HtmlResponse] class is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// an HTML response: one of the views of the [Views] folder
final class HtmlResponse extends ParentResponse
{
    #[\Override]
    public function send(
        Request $request,
        Session $session,
        array $config,
        int $statusCode,
        array $content,
        array $headers = [],
        ?Logger $logger = null
    ): void {
        // the HTML response depends on the status code returned by the controller
        $status = $content["status"];
        // a view corresponds to a status: we look for the 1st view whose list of statuses contains [$status]
        // if no view fits, it is an unexpected error: we display the errors view
        $view = array_find_key(
            $config["views"],
            fn(array $statuses): bool => in_array($status, $statuses, true)
        ) ?? $config["view-errors"];
        // we execute the view: what it writes is put in a buffer instead of being sent to the client
        // the view has access to the variables [$request, $session, $config, $content] of the method
        ob_start();
        require __DIR__ . "/../Views/$view";
        // we retrieve the content of the buffer, the HTML document, and we empty the buffer
        $html = ob_get_clean();
        // sending the response by the parent class
        $this->sendResponse($statusCode, $html, "text/html", $headers);
        // JSON log of the controller's response, without the HTML
        $this->log($logger, $content);
    }
}

Comments

  • line 26: The view to be displayed depends on the status code returned by the controller that processed the action. This code is in [$content["status"]];
  • Lines 29–32: The application configuration is searched for the view that corresponds to this status. The function [array_find_key] (PHP 8.4) returns the key of the first element in the array [$config["views"]] that satisfies the condition expressed by the arrowed function—in this case, the name of the first view whose list of states contains [$status]. If no element satisfies the condition, it returns [null]: this indicates an abnormal status code for the application HTML, and the error view is displayed using the operator [??]. The script PHP 7 performed this search using a fifteen-line loop [while];
  • lines 35–38: the code PHP from the selected view is executed, and the result is stored in the variable [$html]. This code warrants some explanation. Let’s imagine that the selected view is [view-authentication.php], which displays a web authentication form:
    • Line 35: The function [ob_start] initiates what the documentation refers to as an output delay. Anything written by the operations [print], [echo], or by the text HTML from an included script—and which would normally be sent immediately to the client—is placed in an output buffer (ob) without being sent to the client;
    • Line 36: The view [view-authentication.php] is loaded; this is a dynamic view HTML containing code PHP. Two things then happen. First, the PHP code in the view is executed. The result is a page that contains only HTML, or even CSS and JavaScript, but no longer PHP. Next, this HTML code is normally sent to the client. This is actually the case for any text encountered by the PHP interpreter that is not PHP code. Due to the output delay, this code HTML is placed in the output buffer without being sent to the client;
    • Line 38: The [ob_get_clean] function does two things: it returns the contents of the output buffer—that is, the HTML page that was placed there—and it clears the buffer and stops the output delay. From the client’s perspective, it’s as if nothing had happened: it still hasn’t received anything;
  • The view is included by the [send] method: The view's code therefore has access to the method's local variables, specifically its parameters [$request], [$session], [$config], and [$content]. This is how the view receives the data it needs to display;
  • [__DIR__] is the absolute path to the folder containing the currently running script, in this case the [Responses] folder. To find the view, you must therefore go up one level to [..] and then enter the [Views] folder;
  • Line 40: The parent class sends the response to the client, with the type [text/html];
  • line 42: the response [$content] provided by the secondary controller that processed the current action is logged as JSON, without the HTML.

docs.title: 23.12.6. [curl] Tests
docs.text:
To truly test the session’s HTML mode, we would need to review all the views. We’ll do that later. For now, we’ll simply verify that a successful [init-session] action (status 700) in a new [html]-type session does indeed produce a HTML response. According to the configuration file, the view [view-authentication.php] is the response:

> curl -D - -o view.html -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/main.php?action=init-session&type=html"
HTTP/1.0 200 OK
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 16:51:53 GMT
Server: Apache/2.4.58
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Cache-Control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate
Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=60bf588b0873f085af3b33940c0d8417; path=/
Cache-Control: no-cache, private
Vary: Accept-Encoding
Connection: close
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
  • Line 1: The [-D -] option instructs [curl] to write the HTTP headers of the response to standard output (the [-] file), the [-o view.html] option to write the body of the response to the [view.html] file;
  • Line 11: The response is a HTML document.

When opened in a browser, the file [view.html] displays the authentication view, which is shown below.

docs.title: 23.13.1. Overview of Views
docs.text:
The HTML web application uses four views. The authentication view:

The tax calculation view:

The simulation list view:

Unexpected Errors View:

The views use the CSS [Bootstrap] framework, version 5.3. Course PHP 7 used version 4.1: some classes CSS have changed or been removed; we’ll point these out as we go. We’ll describe these views one by one.

docs.title: 23.13.2.1. Overview of the View
docs.text:
The authentication view is as follows:

The view consists of three elements that we’ll call fragments:

  • the top banner, with the logo and title, is generated by the script [v-banner.php];
  • the authentication form is generated by the script [v-authentication.php];
  • the pink error box, displayed only when there are errors, is generated by the script [v-errors.php].

The authentication view is generated by the following page, [view-authentication.php]:

<?php
// the authentication view - statuses [700, 221, 400]
// we inherit the variables of the [HtmlResponse::send] method which does the [require] of this view:
// Request $request: the current request
// Session $session: the application's session
// array $config: the application's configuration
// array $content: the controller's response [action, status, response]

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;

// we compute the view's model
$model = getModelForThisView($request, $content);

function getModelForThisView(Request $request, array $content): stdClass
{
    // the model depends on the application's status
    return match ($content["status"]) {
        // failed authentication: we redisplay the identifier entered and an error message
        221 => (object) [
            "login" => $request->request->getString("user"),
            "errorsTitle" => "The following errors occurred:",
            "errors" => ["Authentication failed"],
        ],
        // 700, 400: empty form, without errors
        default => (object) ["login" => "", "errors" => []],
    };
}
?>
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <!-- UTF-8 encoded document, displayed over the full width of the screen -->
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    <!-- Bootstrap 5.3 -->
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.8/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css"
          integrity="sha384-sRIl4kxILFvY47J16cr9ZwB07vP4J8+LH7qKQnuqkuIAvNWLzeN8tE5YBujZqJLB" crossorigin="anonymous">
    <title>Tax application</title>
</head>
<body>
<div class="container">
    <!-- banner -->
    <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-banner.php" ?>
    <!-- authentication form on 9 columns -->
    <div class="row">
        <div class="col-md-9">
            <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-authentication.php" ?>
        </div>
    </div>
    <!-- if there are errors, we display them below the form -->
    <?php if ($model->errors !== []): ?>
        <div class="row">
            <div class="col-md-9">
                <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-errors.php" ?>
            </div>
        </div>
    <?php endif ?>
</div>
</body>
</html>

Comments

  • lines 2–7: The view is executed by the [require] statement in the [HtmlResponse::send] method. It inherits the variables from this method;
  • lines 13–28: The PHP section of the view calculates the view model. We’ll come back to this a little later;
  • line 30: a HTML5 document begins with this line;
  • lines 31–61: the HTML page is enclosed within the [<html>] and [</html>] tags. The [lang] attribute specifies the document’s language;
  • lines 32–40: header (head) of the HTML document:
    • line 34: the [<meta charset>] tag indicates that the document is encoded in UTF-8;
    • Line 35: The [<meta name="viewport">] tag sets the initial display of the view: across the full width of the screen displaying it (width) at its initial size (initial-scale). The value [shrink-to-fit=no] from version PHP 7 is no longer used with current browsers;
    • Lines 37–38: The [<link rel="stylesheet">] tag specifies the CSS file that governs the view’s appearance. We are using the CSS [Bootstrap] 5.3.8 framework, downloaded from the [jsDelivr] ([https://getbootstrap.com/docs/5.3/getting-started/introduction/]) distribution network. The [integrity] attribute contains the file’s fingerprint: the browser rejects the downloaded file if it does not match this fingerprint, which protects the page from file tampering on the distribution network;
    • line 39: the [<title>] tag sets the page title, which is displayed in the browser tab;
  • Lines 41–60: The body of the web page is enclosed within the [<body>] and [</body>] tags;
  • line 42: the [<div>] tag delimits a section of the displayed page. The [class] attributes used in the view all refer to the CSS Bootstrap framework. The [<div class="container">] tag delimits a Bootstrap container, centered on the page;
  • line 44: the [v-banner.php] fragment is included, which generates the page header. We’ll describe it shortly. The path is constructed using [__DIR__], the [Views] folder: a simple relative path such as ["v-banner.php"] would first be searched for in the directories specified by the [include_path] directive (PHP), then in the calling script’s folder ([Responses]) and the current folder, which can lead to unexpected results;
  • Lines 46–47: The [<div class="row">] tag delimits a Bootstrap row. These rows consist of 12 columns. The [<div class="col-md-9">] tag delimits a section of 9 columns;
  • line 48: the fragment [v-authentication.php] is included, which displays the authentication form;
  • lines 52–58: if the model’s error list is not empty, the fragment [v-errors.php] is included, which displays the errors in a new Bootstrap row. Here, we use the alternative syntax for control structures in PHP, [if (...):] ... [endif], which is more readable than curly braces in a HTML page. The PHP 7 script wrote the error code using the HTML syntax ([heredoc]) ([print <<<EOT ... EOT;]).

Let’s note the dynamic elements to be defined in this code:

  • [$model->errors]: the list of error messages, empty if there are no errors;
  • [$model->errorsTitle]: the text preceding the list of errors.

docs.title: 23.13.2.2. The fragment [v-banner.php]
docs.text:
The fragment [v-banner.php] displays the top banner on all views of the web application:

<?php
// fragment: the top banner of all the views
// model: [$model->logo] (optional) - the URL of the logo, relative to the URL of the displayed page
?>
<!-- banner: a light grey frame with rounded corners -->
<div class="p-4 my-4 bg-body-tertiary rounded-3">
    <div class="row align-items-center">
        <div class="col-md-4">
            <img src="<?= htmlspecialchars($model->logo ?? "Views/logo.jpg") ?>" alt="Cherry tree in bloom">
        </div>
        <div class="col-md-8">
            <h1>Calculate your tax</h1>
        </div>
    </div>
</div>

Comments

  • Line 6: The header is wrapped in a section whose Bootstrap classes provide inner spacing (p-4), vertical margins (my-4), a light gray background (bg-body-tertiary), and rounded corners (rounded-3). Course PHP 7 used the Bootstrap 4 class [jumbotron], which no longer exists in Bootstrap 5: these four classes replace it;
  • line 7: a Bootstrap row. The [align-items-center] class vertically centers the content of its columns;
  • lines 8–10: a [<img>] image is placed in the first four columns of the row;
  • line 9: the syntax [<?= expression ?>] is equivalent to [<?php echo expression ?>]. In other words, the value of the [src] attribute will be the value of the expression PHP. This is:
    • [$model->logo ?? "Views/logo.jpg"]: the URL of the logo, if the view model contains one; otherwise, the URL relative to [Views/logo.jpg]. All URL in the application are of the form [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/main.php?action=…]: the URL relative to [Views/logo.jpg] is supplemented by the browser with the path of the displayed page, resulting in [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/Views/logo.jpg]. The PHP 7 fragment constructed the absolute URL of the logo from server variables ([REQUEST_SCHEME], [SERVER_NAME], [SERVER_PORT], [REQUEST_URI]) and a regular expression: this was unnecessary;
    • [htmlspecialchars(...)]: The function [htmlspecialchars] replaces the special characters in HTML with their entities: [&] becomes [&], [<] becomes [<], [>] becomes [>], ["] becomes ["], and ['] becomes [']. Thus, the value written to the page cannot break the [src] attribute or insert tags into the page;
  • Lines 11–13: The other 8 columns in the row (note that there are 12 in total) are used to display text in large font (tag [<h1>]).

Dynamic element: [$model->logo], the URL for the image displayed in the banner (optional).

Any dynamic value written to a HTML page must go through [htmlspecialchars]. This is the protection against XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) attacks: if a value entered by the user, or originating from an untrusted source, were written as-is into the page, a malicious user could inject code—such as [<script>…</script>]—which would be executed by the browsers of those viewing the page. Version 7 of PHP did not escape any values. Starting with version 8.1 of PHP, the default options for [htmlspecialchars] ([ENT_QUOTES | ENT_SUBSTITUTE | ENT_HTML401]) also encode the apostrophe: calling [htmlspecialchars($value)] is sufficient, whether the value is written in text or in an attribute delimited by quotation marks or apostrophes.

docs.title: 23.13.2.3. The fragment [v-authentication.php]
docs.text:
The fragment [v-authentication.php] displays the web application’s authentication form:

<?php
// fragment: the authentication form
// model: [$model->login] - the identifier to display in the [user] input field
?>
<!-- HTML form - its values are posted with the [authenticate-user] action -->
<form method="post" action="main.php?action=authenticate-user">
    <!-- title on a blue background -->
    <div class="alert alert-primary" role="alert">
        <h4>Please authenticate</h4>
    </div>
    <!-- 1st row: the identifier -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <!-- label on 3 columns -->
        <label for="user" class="col-md-3 col-form-label">User name</label>
        <!-- text input field on 4 columns -->
        <div class="col-md-4">
            <input type="text" class="form-control" id="user" name="user"
                   placeholder="User name" value="<?= htmlspecialchars($model->login) ?>">
        </div>
    </div>
    <!-- 2nd row: the password -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <label for="password" class="col-md-3 col-form-label">Password</label>
        <!-- hidden input field -->
        <div class="col-md-4">
            <input type="password" class="form-control" id="password" name="password"
                   placeholder="Password">
        </div>
    </div>
    <!-- 3rd row: [submit] button -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <div class="col-md-2">
            <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Submit</button>
        </div>
    </div>
</form>

Comments

  • Lines 6–36: The [<form>] tag delimits a HTML form. This form generally has the following characteristics:
    • It defines input fields ([<input>] tags);
    • it has a [submit]-type button that submits the entered values to the URL specified in the [action] attribute of the [<form>] tag. The HTTP method used to query this URL is specified in the [method] attribute of the [<form>] tag;
    • here, when the user clicks the [Submit] button, the browser will submit the values entered in the form to the URL and [main.php?action=authenticate-user];
    • The posted values are the values entered by the user in the two input fields. They will be posted in the form [user=xx&password=yy]. The parameter names [user, password] correspond to the attributes [name] of the input fields;
  • lines 8–10: a Bootstrap section to display a title on a blue background;
  • lines 12–20: the first line of the form. The class [mb-3] adds a bottom margin to the line. Bootstrap 4 used the class [form-group], which no longer exists in Bootstrap 5;
  • Line 14: the label, in three columns. The [for] attribute of the [<label>] tag links the label to the [id] attribute of the input field: clicking on the label places the cursor in the input field;
  • line 16: the input field is placed within a four-column layout;
  • Lines 17–18: The HTML [<input>] tag defines an input field. It has several attributes:
    • [type="text"]: This is a text input field. You can type anything into it;
    • [class="form-control"]: Bootstrap style for the input field;
    • [id="user"]: ID of the input field. This ID is generally used by CSS and the code JavaScript;
    • [name="user"]: name of the input field. The value entered by the user will be submitted by the browser under this name ([user=xx]);
    • [placeholder="prompt"]: the text displayed in the input field when the user has not yet typed anything;
    • [value="value"]: the text displayed in the input field as soon as it appears on the screen, before the user enters anything. This mechanism is used in the event of an error to display the input that caused the error. Here, this value will be the value of [$model->login], escaped by [htmlspecialchars]: an entered identifier containing a quotation mark cannot close the [value] attribute;
  • lines 22–29: similar code for the password entry field. The [type="password"] attribute creates a text input field where the characters being typed are hidden;
  • lines 31–35: a third line for the [Submit] button;
  • line 33: because it has the attribute [type="submit"], clicking this button triggers the browser to send the entered values to the server. The classes CSS and [btn btn-primary] display a blue button.

There is one last thing to explain. The [action="main.php?action=authenticate-user"] attribute of the [<form>] tag defines an incomplete URL (it does not begin with http://machine:port/path). The authentication view will be obtained using various URL entries:

  • [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/main.php?action=init-session&type=html];
  • [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/main.php?action=authenticate-user].

These URL files refer to a [main.php] document located at the path [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12]. This will be the case for all URL files in this application. The URL and [main.php?action=authenticate-user] files will be prefixed with this path when the entered values are sent. These values will therefore be posted to the URL and [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/main.php?action=authenticate-user] files.

docs.title: 23.13.2.4. The [v-errors.php] fragment
docs.text:
The fragment [v-errors.php] displays a list of error messages. It is used by three of the application’s four views:

<?php
// fragment: a list of error messages in a pink frame
// model: [$model->errorsTitle] - the introductory text, [$model->errors] - the messages
?>
<div class="alert alert-danger" role="alert">
    <?= htmlspecialchars($model->errorsTitle) ?>
    <ul class="mb-0">
        <?php foreach ($model->errors as $error): ?>
            <li><?= htmlspecialchars($error) ?></li>
        <?php endforeach ?>
    </ul>
</div>
  • Line 5: Errors are displayed in a Bootstrap container with a pink background;
  • line 6: the text introducing the errors;
  • lines 7–11: the HTML [<ul>] tag (unordered list) displays a bulleted list. Each list item has the syntax [<li>item</li>]. The class [mb-0] removes the bottom margin from the list;
  • Lines 8–10: the alternative syntax for the loop [foreach]. Each message is escaped by [htmlspecialchars]: controller error messages contain the values sent by the client ([invalid value [x] for parameter [children]]). In course PHP 7, the view model contained the list HTML of errors, constructed by concatenating strings [<li>$error</li>]: A posted value containing code JavaScript would have been executed by the browser.

Dynamic elements: [$model->errorsTitle] and [$model->errors].

docs.title: 23.13.2.5. Visual testing
docs.text:
We can test the views well before integrating them into the application. The goal here is to test their visual appearance. We gather all the test views in the [Tests] folder of the project. To test the [view-authentication.php] view, we need to create the data model it will display. The script [Tests/view-authentication.php] is as follows:

<?php
// visual test of the authentication view: the view is displayed with a test model

// we compute the view's model
$model = getModelForThisView();

function getModelForThisView(): stdClass
{
    return (object) [
        // the user's identifier
        "login" => "albert",
        // list of errors - the 2nd one checks that the special HTML characters are neutralized
        "errorsTitle" => "The following errors occurred:",
        "errors" => ["error1", "<b>error2</b>"],
        // the banner's logo, relative to the URL of this script
        "logo" => "../Views/logo.jpg",
    ];
}
?>
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.8/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css"
          integrity="sha384-sRIl4kxILFvY47J16cr9ZwB07vP4J8+LH7qKQnuqkuIAvNWLzeN8tE5YBujZqJLB" crossorigin="anonymous">
    <title>Tax application</title>
</head>
<body>
<div class="container">
    <!-- banner -->
    <?php require __DIR__ . "/../Views/v-banner.php" ?>
    <!-- authentication form on 9 columns -->
    <div class="row">
        <div class="col-md-9">
            <?php require __DIR__ . "/../Views/v-authentication.php" ?>
        </div>
    </div>
    <!-- if there are errors, we display them below the form -->
    <?php if ($model->errors !== []): ?>
        <div class="row">
            <div class="col-md-9">
                <?php require __DIR__ . "/../Views/v-errors.php" ?>
            </div>
        </div>
    <?php endif ?>
</div>
</body>
</html>

Comments

  • Line 5: The authentication view contains dynamic parts controlled by the [$model] object. This object is called the view model. According to one of the two definitions given for the acronym MVC, this is the M in MVC. It is calculated by the function [getModelForThisView]. A function defined at the top level of a script is known as soon as the script begins execution: it can be called before it is defined;
  • lines 9–17: The view model is an object of type [stdClass], the generic class of PHP. It is obtained here by converting an associative array into an object using the [(object)] operator: the array keys become the object’s attributes. The type [stdClass] is the only object type to which undeclared attributes can still be added (see the chapter on classes). An associative array could have been used instead to achieve the same result;
  • line 14: test values for the view’s dynamic elements. The second error contains HTML tags: we’ll verify that they are displayed as-is and not interpreted by the browser;
  • line 16: the URL for the logo is relative to the URL for the test script, located in the [Tests] folder;
  • line 32: the rest of the script is from the [Views/view-authentication.php] view. The included fragments are those from the [Views] folder: these are the ones being tested. Course PHP 7 copied a version of them into the [Tests] folder.

The visual test is performed by requesting the URL and [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/Tests/view-authentication.php] files in a browser:

Note that the [<b>] tag from the second error was displayed but not interpreted: the protection against XSS attacks is working. Continue these visual tests until you are satisfied with the result. During debugging, we modify the file in [VS Code] and then refresh the browser page (F5).

docs.title: 23.13.2.6. Calculating the View Model
docs.text:
Once the visual appearance of the view has been determined, we can proceed to calculate the view model under real-world conditions. Let’s review the status codes that lead to this view. They can be found in the configuration file:

    "views": {
        "view-authentication.php": [700, 221, 400],
        "view-tax-calculation.php": [200, 300, 341, 350, 800],
        "view-simulations-list.php": [500, 600]
    },
    "view-errors": "view-errors.php"

Therefore, the status codes [700, 221, 400] cause the authentication view to be displayed. To determine the meaning of these codes, we can refer to the [curl] tests performed on the JSON application:

  • 700 is the status code following a successful [init-session] action: the blank authentication form is then displayed;
  • 221 is the status code following a failed [authenticate-user] action (unrecognized credentials): the authentication form is then displayed so that the credentials can be corrected;
  • 400 is the status code following a successful [end-session] action: the empty authentication form is then displayed.

Now that we know when the authentication form should be displayed, we can calculate its model in [view-authentication.php]:

<?php
// the authentication view - statuses [700, 221, 400]
// we inherit the variables of the [HtmlResponse::send] method which does the [require] of this view:
// Request $request: the current request
// Session $session: the application's session
// array $config: the application's configuration
// array $content: the controller's response [action, status, response]

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;

// we compute the view's model
$model = getModelForThisView($request, $content);

function getModelForThisView(Request $request, array $content): stdClass
{
    // the model depends on the application's status
    return match ($content["status"]) {
        // failed authentication: we redisplay the identifier entered and an error message
        221 => (object) [
            "login" => $request->request->getString("user"),
            "errorsTitle" => "The following errors occurred:",
            "errors" => ["Authentication failed"],
        ],
        // 700, 400: empty form, without errors
        default => (object) ["login" => "", "errors" => []],
    };
}
?>

Comments

  • lines 3–7: We declare the variables inherited from the [HtmlResponse::send] method, which renders the view using [require];
  • line 10: the Symfony class used in the view code. The view has no namespace: without this statement, [Request] would refer to the class [\Request], which does not exist;
  • Lines 15–28: The [getModelForThisView] function calculates the view model. It receives the request and response from the controller—the only data it needs. The views do not have a [declare(strict_types=1)] declaration: they are HTML pages with some PHP code;
  • lines 18–27: The model depends on the status code returned by the controller that processed the current action:
    • lines 20–23: in the case of failed authentication: the username entered by the user, found in the posted parameters [$request->request], is redisplayed, and an error message is shown. The user can then try another authentication attempt;
    • line 26: status codes 700 and 400: a blank authentication form, with no errors.

Script PHP 7 used a statement that modified an object created at the beginning of the function.

docs.title: 23.13.2.8. Conclusion
docs.text:
We were able to test the view [view-authentication.php] without having written the other views. This was possible because:

  • all the controllers have been written;
  • [curl] allows us to send requests to the server without needing the views. When writing controllers, you must be aware that anyone can do this. You must therefore be prepared to handle requests that no view would allow. These are created manually using [curl]. You should never assume a priori that “this request is impossible.” You must verify it.

docs.title: 23.13.3.1. Overview of the view
docs.text:
The tax calculation view is as follows:

The view has five parts:

  • the top banner is generated by the fragment [v-banner.php], which has already been presented;
  • the tax calculation form is generated by the fragment [v-tax-calculation.php];
  • a menu with two links is generated by the fragment [v-menu.php];
  • the calculation result is displayed in a green box;
  • Errors are displayed in a pink box by the fragment [v-errors.php].

The green and pink frames are never displayed together in the application: the screenshot above is from the visual test of the view, presented later. The tax calculation view is generated by the following script, [view-tax-calculation.php], of which we are currently showing only the section HTML:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">

    <title>Tax application</title>
</head>
<body>
<div class="container">
    <!-- banner -->
    <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-banner.php" ?>
    <!-- two-column row: the menu on 3 columns, the form on 9 columns -->

            <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-menu.php" ?>
        </div>
        <div class="col-md-9">
            <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-tax-calculation.php" ?>
        </div>
    </div>
    <!-- success: the calculation result in a green frame, below the form -->
    <?php if ($model->results !== []): ?>
        <div class="row">
            <div class="col-md-9 offset-md-3">
                <div class="alert alert-success" role="alert">
                    <?php foreach ($model->results as $line): ?>
                        <?= htmlspecialchars($line) ?><br>
                    <?php endforeach ?>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    <?php endif ?>

    <?php if ($model->errors !== []): ?>

                <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-errors.php" ?>
            </div>
