Comments

We will only comment on the new features:

  • line 57: inclusion of the top banner of the view;
  • lines 60–62: inclusion of the menu, which will occupy three columns of the Bootstrap row following the header;
  • lines 63–65: inclusion of the tax calculation form, which will occupy the remaining nine columns of this row;
  • lines 68–78: if the tax calculation was successful, the list [$model->results] is not empty, and the calculation result is displayed in a green frame (class [alert-success]). Each line of the result is followed by a line break ([<br>]). The box is on a new Bootstrap line and occupies nine columns offset by three columns (class [offset-md-3]). It will therefore appear immediately below the tax calculation form. Script PHP 7 achieved the offset using an empty column [<div class="col-md-3"></div>];
  • lines 80–86: if the tax calculation failed, the list [$model->errors] is not empty, and the errors are displayed in a pink box in the same location by the fragment [v-errors.php].

docs.title: 23.13.3.2. The fragment [v-tax-calculation.php]
docs.text:
The fragment [v-tax-calculation.php] displays the tax calculation form:

<?php
// fragment: the tax calculation form
// model: [$model->married] (yes / no), [$model->children], [$model->salary] - the displayed values
?>
<!-- HTML form posted with the [calculate-tax] action -->
<form method="post" action="main.php?action=calculate-tax">
    <!-- title on a blue background -->
    <div class="alert alert-primary" role="alert">
        <h4>Fill in the form below and then submit it</h4>
    </div>
    <!-- 1st row: the marital status, two radio buttons of the same [married] group -->
    <fieldset class="row mb-3">
        <legend class="col-form-label col-md-4 pt-0">Are you married or in a civil partnership?</legend>
        <div class="col-md-5">
            <div class="form-check">
                <input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="married" id="marriedYes" value="yes"
                    <?= $model->married === "yes" ? "checked" : "" ?>>
                <label class="form-check-label" for="marriedYes">Yes</label>
            </div>
            <div class="form-check">
                <input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="married" id="marriedNo" value="no"
                    <?= $model->married === "yes" ? "" : "checked" ?>>
                <label class="form-check-label" for="marriedNo">No</label>
            </div>
        </div>
    </fieldset>
    <!-- 2nd row: the number of children, an integer >= 0 -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <label for="children" class="col-md-4 col-form-label">Number of dependent children</label>
        <div class="col-md-5">
            <input type="number" min="0" step="1" class="form-control" id="children" name="children"
                   placeholder="Number of dependent children" value="<?= htmlspecialchars($model->children) ?>">
        </div>
    </div>
    <!-- 3rd row: the annual salary, an integer >= 0 -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <label for="salary" class="col-md-4 col-form-label">Annual salary</label>
        <div class="col-md-5">
            <input type="number" min="0" step="1" class="form-control" id="salary" name="salary"
                   placeholder="Annual salary" aria-describedby="salaryHelp"
                   value="<?= htmlspecialchars($model->salary) ?>">
            <div id="salaryHelp" class="form-text">Round down to the nearest euro</div>
        </div>
    </div>
    <!-- 4th row: [submit] button -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <div class="col-md-5">
            <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Submit</button>
        </div>
    </div>
</form>

Comments

  • Line 6: The form HTML will be posted (attribute [method]) to URL and [main.php?action=calculate-tax] (attribute [action]). The posted values will be the values from the input fields:
    • the value of the selected radio button in the form [married=yes] if the [Yes] radio button is selected, or [married=no] if the [No] radio button is selected. [married] is the value of the [name] attribute for both radio buttons, [yes] and [no] are the values of their [value] attributes;
    • the value of the numeric input field [children] in the form [children=xx], where [xx] is the value entered by the user via the keyboard;
    • the value of the numeric input field [salary] in the form [salary=xx];
    • finally, the posted value will be in the form [married=xx&children=yy&salary=zz];
  • The entered values will be posted when the user clicks the button labeled [Submit] on line 48;
  • Lines 12–26: the two radio buttons. The [<fieldset>] tag groups form elements together, and the [<legend>] tag provides them with a title;
  • lines 16–21: these are radio buttons because of the [type="radio"] attribute. The two radio buttons are part of the same radio button group because they share the same [name] attribute. The browser ensures that, within a group of radio buttons, only one is selected at any given time. Therefore, clicking one deselects the one that was previously selected;
  • lines 17–22: When the form is displayed, one of the radio buttons must be selected; to achieve this, simply add the [checked] attribute to the relevant [<input type="radio">] tag. The ternary operator sets this attribute on the [Yes] button if [$model->married] equals [yes]; otherwise, it sets it on the [No] button. Since the value being written is a constant, there is nothing to escape. Course PHP 7 inserted two variables, [checkedYes] and [checkedNo], into the model, containing the text [checked="checked"] or an empty string;
  • lines 31–32: a numeric input field ([type="number"]) with a minimum value of 0 ([min="0"]). In modern browsers, this means the user can only enter a number greater than or equal to 0. The input can also be made using a slider that can be clicked to increase or decrease the value. The attribute [step="1"] indicates that the slider operates in increments of 1: the slider will only accept integer values ranging from 0 to n in steps of 1. For manual entry, this means that numbers with decimals will not be accepted. In certain views, the children’s input field must be pre-filled with the last entry made in that field: this is the role of the attribute [value], whose value is provided by [$model->children];
  • Lines 39–42: The same explanations apply to salary entry as to those for children. The tooltip below the input field has the class [form-text]; Bootstrap 4 used the tag [<small>].

Dynamic elements: [$model->married], [$model->children], [$model->salary].

docs.title: 23.13.3.3. The [v-menu.php] snippet
docs.text:
This fragment displays a menu to the left of the tax calculation form. Its code is as follows:

<?php
// fragment: the application's menu
// model: [$model->menuOptions] - an array [link text => target URL]
?>
<!-- Bootstrap menu: a vertical list of links -->
<nav class="nav flex-column">
    <?php foreach ($model->menuOptions as $text => $url): ?>
        <a class="nav-link" href="<?= htmlspecialchars($url) ?>"><?= htmlspecialchars($text) ?></a>
    <?php endforeach ?>
</nav>

Comments

  • Lines 6–10: The HTML and [<nav>] tags enclose a section of the document containing navigation links to other documents. The [nav, flex-column, nav-link] classes are Bootstrap classes that define the menu’s appearance: a vertical list of links;
  • line 7: the [$model->menuOptions] model for the fragment is an array of the form [["List of simulations" => "main.php?action=list-simulations", "End of session" => "main.php?action=end-session"]];
  • line 8: the HTML [<a>] tag introduces a navigation link. [$url] is the URL that is navigated to when the [$text] link is clicked. The browser then performs a [GET $url] operation. If [$url] is a relative URL, then it is supplemented by the path of the URL currently displayed by the browser. Thus, while the browser’s current URL is of type [http://path/main.php?parameters], the [List of simulations] link leads to [http://path/main.php?action=list-simulations]. The text and the URL are escaped by [htmlspecialchars]: in a URL, the character [&] that separates the parameters must be written as [&] in a HTML document.

docs.title: 23.13.3.4. Visual test
docs.text:
We create a test script for view [view-tax-calculation.php] in folder [Tests]:

<?php
// visual test of the tax calculation view: the view is displayed with a test model

// we compute the view's model
$model = getModelForThisView();

function getModelForThisView(): stdClass
{
    return (object) [
        // form
        "married" => "no",

docs.title: 23.13.3.5. Calculating the View Model
docs.text:
Once the visual appearance of the view has been determined, you can proceed to calculate the view model under real-world conditions. The status codes that lead to this view are the [200, 300, 341, 350, 800] codes in the configuration. To determine the meaning of these codes, you can refer to the [curl] tests performed on the JSON application:

  • 200 is the status code following a successful [authenticate-user] action: the blank tax calculation form is then displayed;
  • 300 is the status code following a successful [calculate-tax] action. The calculation form is then displayed with the data entered and the tax amount. The user can then perform another calculation;
  • 341 is the status code returned for a tax calculation with valid parameters when a lack of connection to the DBMS causes an error;
  • 350 is the status code returned for a tax calculation with valid parameters when a failure to connect to the [Redis] server causes an error;
  • Status code 800 will be discussed later. We have not encountered it yet;
  • We assume here that the user is using a modern browser. Thus, with the form under consideration, it is not possible to enter negative numbers, non-numeric character strings, or decimal numbers in the [children, salary] input fields. If these errors occur nonetheless (in a manually crafted request), they will be treated as unexpected errors: in that case, the view [view-errors.php] will be displayed.

Now that we know when the tax calculation form should be displayed, we can define its model in [view-tax-calculation.php]:

<?php
// the tax calculation view - statuses [200, 300, 341, 350, 800]
// we inherit the variables [$request, $session, $config, $content] of the [HtmlResponse::send] method

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;

// we compute the view's model
$model = getModelForThisView($request, $content);

function getModelForThisView(Request $request, array $content): stdClass
{
    $model = new stdClass();
    // application status
    $status = $content["status"];
    // the form: empty (200, 800) or restored with the values entered (300, 341, 350)
    $entered = in_array($status, [300, 341, 350], true);
    $model->married = $entered ? $request->request->getString("married") : "no";
    $model->children = $entered ? $request->request->getString("children") : "";
    $model->salary = $entered ? $request->request->getString("salary") : "";
    // successful calculation (300): the controller's response is a [Simulation] object
    $model->results = [];
    if ($status === 300) {
        $simulation = $content["response"];
        $model->results = [
            "Tax amount: $simulation->tax euros",
            "Discount: $simulation->discount euros",
            "Reduction: $simulation->reduction euros",
            "Surcharge: $simulation->surcharge euros",
            "Tax rate: " . $simulation->rate * 100 . " %",
        ];
    }
    // failed calculation (341: database unavailable, 350: Redis unavailable)
    $model->errorsTitle = "The following error occurred:";
    $model->errors = in_array($status, [341, 350], true) ? [$content["response"]] : [];
    // the menu
    $model->menuOptions = [
        "List of simulations" => "main.php?action=list-simulations",
        "End of session" => "main.php?action=end-session",
    ];
    // we return the model
    return $model;
}
?>

Comments

  • line 17: For statuses 300, 341, and 350, the form is redisplayed with the entered values;
  • Lines 18–20: The entered values are found in the posted parameters [$request->request]. For statuses 200 and 800, the form is empty, with the [No] button checked;
  • Lines 23–32: Successful tax calculation. The response from the [$content["response"]] controller is a [Simulation] object: the result lines are constructed based on its attributes. The rate is displayed as a percentage. Since a simulation is an object, [$simulation->tax] is interpolated directly into a string enclosed in quotation marks;
  • line 35: case where the tax calculation fails due to the database or server being unavailable ([Redis]). The controller’s response is then the error message;
  • Lines 37–40: the two menu options.

The fragment [v-simulations-list.php] is as follows:

<?php
// fragment: the table of simulations
// model: [$model->simulations] - the list of [Simulation] objects to display
?>
<!-- title on a blue background -->
<div class="alert alert-primary" role="alert">
    <h4>List of your simulations</h4>
</div>
<!-- table of simulations -->
<table class="table table-sm table-hover table-striped">

    <?php foreach ($model->simulations as $i => $simulation): ?>

            <!-- the simulation no. is the header of the row -->
            <th scope="row"><?= $i ?></th>
            <td><?= htmlspecialchars($simulation->married) ?></td>
            <td><?= $simulation->children ?></td>
            <td><?= $simulation->salary ?></td>
            <td><?= $simulation->tax ?></td>
            <td><?= $simulation->surcharge ?></td>
            <td><?= $simulation->discount ?></td>
            <td><?= $simulation->reduction ?></td>

Comments

  • Lines 10–45: A table named HTML is created using the [<table>] tag. Bootstrap classes give it a compact appearance (table-sm), a highlighted row when the mouse hovers over it (table-hover), and alternating row colors (table-striped);
  • Lines 12–25: The table column headers are defined within a ***[<thead>]*** (table head) tag. The ***[<tr>] (table row) tag defines a row. The [<th>] tag (table header) defines a column header. There are ten of them. [scope="col"] indicates that the header applies to the column. [scope="row"]* indicates that the header applies to the row;
  • lines 27–44: the [<tbody>] tag encloses the data displayed by the table;
  • line 28: the list of simulations is found in the [$model->simulations] model. It is a list of [Simulation] objects: [$i] is the simulation number in the list;

  • lines 32–39: each [<td>] tag defines a column in the row. Only the marital status—a string of characters—is escaped: the other attributes of the simulation are numbers, typed as such in the [Simulation] class, which cannot contain special characters from the HTML class;
  • Line 41: a link to delete the simulation. The URL [main.php?action=delete-simulation&number=$i] takes the number displayed in the first column of the table.

docs.title: 23.13.5. Viewing Unexpected Errors
docs.text:
Here, an unexpected error is defined as an error that should not have occurred during normal use of the web application. Let’s take the following request as an example, in session JSON:

> curl -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/main.php?action=calculate-tax" -d "salary=y"
{"action":"calculate-tax","status":337,"response":["missing parameter [married]","missing parameter [children]","invalid value [y] for parameter [salary]"]}

The parameters [married] and [children] are missing, and the parameter [salary] is invalid. However, in the HTML form of the web application, this situation cannot occur:

  • all parameters are present;
  • the parameter [married], which derives its value from the [value] attributes of two radio buttons, must be either [yes] or [no];
  • with a modern browser, the [<input type="number" min="0" step="1" …>] attributes ensure that the entries for children and salary are necessarily integers >= 0.

However, nothing prevents a user from sending such a request to our server—using [curl] or their browser’s developer tools—during a HTML session. We’ll call an “unexpected error” any error that shouldn’t occur within the HTML application. If it does occur, it’s likely because someone is trying to “hack” the application. For educational purposes, we’ve decided to display an error page for these cases. In reality, we could re-display the last page sent to the client. To do this, we simply need to store the last HTML response sent in the session. In the event of an unexpected error, we return this response. This way, the user will have the impression that the server is not responding to their errors since the displayed page does not change.

It is the missing status codes in the [views] key of the configuration file that cause the unexpected errors view to be displayed. The code for calculating the view model [view-errors.php] is as follows:

<?php

docs.title: 23.13.6. Implementing Application Menu Actions
docs.text:
Here, we will discuss the implementation of menu actions. Let’s review the meanings of the links we’ve encountered:

ViewLinkTargetRoleTax Calculation[List of simulations][main.php?action=list-simulations]Request a list of simulationsTax Calculation[End of session][main.php?action=end-session]Request to end the sessionList of simulations[Tax calculation][main.php?action=display-tax-calculation]Display the tax calculation viewList of simulations[End of session][main.php?action=end-session]Request to end the sessionUnexpected errors[Tax calculation][main.php?action=display-tax-calculation]Display the tax calculation viewUnexpected errors[List of simulations][main.php?action=list-simulations]Request a list of simulationsUnexpected errors[End of session][main.php?action=end-session]Request to end the session

Note that clicking a link triggers a GET to the link’s target. The [list-simulations, end-session] actions have been implemented using a GET operation, which allows us to use them as link targets. When the action is performed via a POST, using a link is no longer possible unless it is combined with a JavaScript.

From the actions listed above, it appears that the [display-tax-calculation] action has not yet been implemented. This is a navigation operation between two views: the JSON or XML server has no reason to implement it because it does not have the concept of a view. It is the HTML server that introduces this concept. We therefore need to implement the action [display-tax-calculation]. This will allow us to review the procedure for implementing an action within the server:

  • we add a case to the [Action] enumeration: [case DisplayTaxCalculation = "display-tax-calculation";];
  • we write the secondary controller [DisplayTaxCalculationController] to the [Controllers] folder;
  • add its file to the [dependencies] key in the [config.json] file;
  • add the branch [Action::DisplayTaxCalculation => new DisplayTaxCalculationController()] to the expression [match] of the main controller;
  • associate the status code returned by the controller, 800, with the tax calculation view in key [views] of [config.json].

The [DisplayTaxCalculationController] controller is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// action [display-tax-calculation]: navigation to the tax calculation view (HTML application)
final class DisplayTaxCalculationController implements InterfaceController
{
    #[\Override]
    public function execute(array $config, Request $request, Session $session): ControllerResult
    {
        // view change: we just return the status code associated with the target view
        return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_OK, 800, "");
    }
}
  • Line 14: Like the other secondary controllers, the new controller implements the [InterfaceController] interface;
  • line 20: View changes are easy to implement: simply set the status code associated with the target view—in this case, code 800. A view change cannot result in an error.

docs.title: 23.13.7. Real-World Testing
docs.text:
The code has been written, and each action has been tested with [curl]. We still need to test the view flow in a real-world scenario. We need a way to initialize the HTML session. We know that we need to send the parameters [action=init-session&type=html] to the server. To avoid having to type them into the browser’s address bar, we’ll add the script [index.php] to our application:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// redirection (code 302) to [main.php] in [html] mode
header("Location: main.php?action=init-session&type=html");
  • Line 6: [header] is a function that adds a HTTP header to the response. The HTTP [Location: main.php?action=init-session&type=html] header instructs the client browser to redirect to the specified URL. PHP then sets the response status to [302 Found].

The [index.php] script is requested along with the URL and [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/index.php] scripts. When the client browser receives the redirect to the relative URL from [main.php?action=init-session&type=html], it will request the absolute URL for [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/main.php?action=init-session&type=html], and the HTML session will begin.

The startup URL can be simplified to [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/]. If no document is specified in URL, [Apache] uses the [index.html] or [index.php] document from the folder. In this case, the script [index.php] will therefore be used. Let’s verify this with [curl]:

> curl -i http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 16:51:53 GMT
Server: Apache/2.4.58
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Location: main.php?action=init-session&type=html
Content-Length: 0
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8
  • Line 2: The code HTTP [302] is a redirect code: the client is told that the requested URL has been moved;
  • Line 6: The new URL is specified by the header [Location]. A browser follows this redirect with a new request for GET. [curl] does so only if given the [-L] option.

In the browser, the developer tools (F12, [Network] tab) show both requests: the first receives a 302 response, and the second displays the authentication page. docs.title: 23.14.1. Client/server architecture
docs.text:
We will now focus on the client JSON [A] of the web service [B]. The client [A], like the web service [B], has a layered structure:

This architecture is reflected in the following code organization within the [scripts-console/tax/version-12] folder:

scripts-console/tax/version-12
├── Business
│   ├── ClientBusiness.php
│   └── InterfaceClientBusiness.php
├── Dao
│   ├── ClientDao.php
│   └── InterfaceClientDao.php
├── Data
│   ├── config.json
│   ├── errors.json
│   ├── results.json
│   └── taxpayersdata.json
├── Main
│   └── main.php
└── Tests
    └── ClientBusinessTest.php

The other classes used by the client have already been discussed and explained. As with previous clients, they are loaded from the folders where they were written:

ClassRole and OriginTaxExceptionThe application's exception class. Version 5, folder [Entities]TaxPayerDataA taxpayer's data [married, children, salary]. Version 5, file [Entities]UtilitiesReading and writing files JSON. Version 5, folder [Utilities]TraitDaoImplementation of methods [getTaxPayersData] and [saveResults]. Version 5, folder [Dao]SimulationA tax calculation simulation. Version 12 server, folder [Entities]

The client uses the server’s class [Simulation]: this is the format in which the server sends its simulations, and this class [readonly] with public attributes is suitable for both the client and the server. The class PHP 7 [BaseEntity], from which the client class [Simulation] 7 PHP was derived, no longer exists.

docs.title: 23.14.2.1. Interface
docs.text:
The interface of layer [dao] is as follows: [Dao/InterfaceClientDao.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the interface of the [dao] layer of the client of the JSON web service of version 12
// all the methods throw a [TaxException] exception in case of error
interface InterfaceClientDao
{
    // reading the taxpayers data (implemented by the trait [TraitDao])
    /** @return TaxPayerData[] */
    public function getTaxPayersData(string $taxPayersFilename, string $errorsFilename): array;

    // saving the results (implemented by the trait [TraitDao])
    /** @param Simulation[] $simulations */
    public function saveResults(string $resultsFilename, array $simulations): void;

    // action [init-session]: start of a session of type json, xml or html
    public function initSession(string $type = "json"): void;

    // action [authenticate-user]
    public function authenticateUser(string $user, #[\SensitiveParameter] string $password): void;

    // action [calculate-tax]: calculation of the tax of a taxpayer
    public function calculateTax(string $married, int $children, int $salary): Simulation;

    // action [list-simulations]: the list of the simulations of the session
    /** @return Simulation[] */
    public function listSimulations(): array;

    // action [delete-simulation]: returns the new list of the simulations
    /** @return Simulation[] */
    public function deleteSimulation(int $number): array;

    // action [end-session]
    public function endSession(): void;
}

Comments

  • Line 14: The [getTaxPayersData] method is used to process the JSON file containing taxpayer data. This method is implemented by the [TraitDao] feature in version 5;
  • Line 18: The [saveResults] method allows you to save the results of multiple tax calculations to a JSON file. Here as well, this method is implemented by the trait [TraitDao]. This trait delegates the work to the method [Utilities::writeJsonFile], which can convert any object into JSON based on its public attributes: [TaxPayerData] objects in previous versions, [Simulation] objects here;
  • lines 21–38: a method has been created for each of the actions accepted by the web service, with the exception of the [display-tax-calculation] action, which is used only by the HTML application;
  • line 24: the [SensitiveParameter] attribute (PHP 8.2), which we’ve already encountered: if an exception is thrown while the method is executing, the password value will not appear in the call trace;
  • the documentation comments (PHPDoc), [@return Simulation[]], and [@param Simulation[] $simulations] specify the contents of the arrays. PHP cannot determine the type of an array’s contents: the type [array] does not specify that the elements are [Simulation] objects. These comments convey this information to the [VS Code] editor (PHP Intelephense extension), which can then suggest the attributes of [Simulation] when traversing the array.

docs.title: 23.14.2.2. Implementation
docs.text:
The [InterfaceClientDao] interface is implemented by the following [ClientDao] class:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpClient\HttpClient;
use Symfony\Contracts\HttpClient\Exception\TransportExceptionInterface;
use Symfony\Contracts\HttpClient\HttpClientInterface;
use Symfony\Contracts\HttpClient\ResponseInterface;

// the [dao] layer of the client of the JSON web service of version 12
// one method per action of the server; the session is maintained with the session cookie
class ClientDao implements InterfaceClientDao
{
    // the trait of version 5 implements the [getTaxPayersData] and [saveResults] methods of the interface
    use TraitDao;

    // the HTTP client
    private readonly HttpClientInterface $httpClient;
    // the session cookie (null as long as the server has not sent it)
    private ?string $sessionCookie = null;

    // constructor
    // $urlServer: the URL of the JSON web service
    // $httpClientOptions: options of the HTTP client (verify_peer, verify_host...)
    // $verbose: if true, the server's responses are displayed on the console
    public function __construct(
        private readonly string $urlServer,
        array $httpClientOptions = [],
        private readonly bool $verbose = true,
    ) {
        $this->httpClient = HttpClient::create($httpClientOptions);
    }

Comments

  • Line 19: The class uses the [TraitDao] trait, which implements two methods of the interface:
    • [getTaxPayersData(string $taxPayersFilename, string $errorsFilename): array];
    • [saveResults(string $resultsFilename, array $simulations): void];
  • Line 22: The Symfony client HTTP is created only once, by the constructor, and is used for all requests. The client PHP used to create a new client HTTP in each method;
  • line 24: the session cookie. Its role was described with the client in version 9. It is set to [null] until the server sends it;
  • Lines 30–34: The constructor receives three parameters, two of which are promoted to attributes:
    • the URL and [$urlServer] from the JSON web service;
    • the [$httpClientOptions] options from the HTTP client. These come from the configuration file: as with version 11, these are the [verify_peer] and [verify_host] options, which would allow working with the self-signed certificate [Laragon] if the server’s URL used the schema [https];
    • a Boolean [$verbose] which, when set to [true], indicates that the class should display the server's responses on the console.

docs.title: The [initSession] method
docs.text:
The [initSession] method is implemented as follows:

    // action [init-session]: it must be the 1st action requested from the server
    #[\Override]
    public function initSession(string $type = "json"): void
    {
        // GET main.php?action=init-session&type=json - the response is a simple message
        $this->sendRequest("GET", ["action" => "init-session", "type" => $type]);
    }

Since action [init-session] is the first action requested from the web service, method [initSession] will be the first method in the [dao] layer to be called.

Comments

  • Line 40: The desired session type is passed as a parameter. If no parameter is provided, a JSON session will be started. A JSON client can request a XML session: it will receive XML responses from version 11, which it will not be able to process;
  • Line 43: A GET request is sent to the web service. Its two parameters are placed in the URL: [main.php?action=init-session&type=json]. The server’s response (a simple message) is not processed. The private method [sendRequest] throws an exception if the response code HTTP is not 200 OK.

The client PHP 7 repeated the following steps in each of its methods: creating the client HTTP, preparing the request options (including the session cookie), and calling the method [getResponse]. We factored this work into the private method [sendRequest].

docs.title: The [sendRequest] method
docs.text:
// sending a request to the server and using its response
    // $method: GET or POST
    // $query: the parameters of the URL
    // $body: the posted parameters (POST only)
    // returns the [response] element of the server's JSON response
    private function sendRequest(string $method, array $query, array $body = []): mixed
    {
        // the options of the request
        $options = ["query" => $query];
        if ($body !== []) {
            // the posted parameters are sent in the form [param1=v1&param2=v2...]
            $options["body"] = $body;
        }
        if ($this->sessionCookie !== null) {
            // we send back to the server the session cookie it sent us
            $options["headers"] = ["Cookie" => $this->sessionCookie];
        }
        // we make the request - the response will only really be read by [getResponse]
        $response = $this->httpClient->request($method, $this->urlServer, $options);
        // we use the response
        return $this->getResponse($response);
    }

Comments

  • line 51: the method receives the HTTP method from the request (GET or POST), the parameters from URL, and, for POST, the posted parameters. The [$body] parameter is optional; its default value is an empty array;
  • line 54: the [query] option of the Symfony client HTTP contains the parameters from URL. Symfony encodes them itself;
  • line 57: when the [body] option is an array, Symfony sends the posted parameters in the form [param1=v1&param2=v2…] with the header [Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded], just as a browser does when posting a form;
  • lines 59–61: Starting with the second request, we send the session cookie back to the server that it sent to us. This is how the server retrieves the client’s session;
  • line 64: the request is prepared. Symfony’s HTTP client is asynchronous: the request is actually sent and the response read when we request the status, headers, or content of the response, which is what the [getResponse] method does;
  • line 66: the [response] element of the server’s response is returned.

docs.title: The [getResponse] method
docs.text:
The [getResponse] method is responsible for processing the web service response:

    // using the server's response
    // returns the [response] element of the JSON response {"action": ..., "status": ..., "response": ...}
    private function getResponse(ResponseInterface $response): mixed
    {
        try {
            // the status, the headers and the JSON document of the response, even in case of error (parameter false)
            $statusCode = $response->getStatusCode();
            $headers = $response->getHeaders(false);
            $json = $response->getContent(false);
        } catch (TransportExceptionInterface $ex) {
            // the server could not be reached
            throw new TaxException("Error communicating with the server ({$ex->getMessage()})", 40, $ex);
        }
        // logs
        if ($this->verbose) {
            print "$json\n";
        }
        // the session cookie: we keep the last one sent by the server
        // (the [end-session] action deletes the old cookie and sends a new one)
        foreach ($headers["set-cookie"] ?? [] as $cookie) {
            if (preg_match('/^PHPSESSID=([^;]+)/', $cookie, $fields) === 1) {
                $this->sessionCookie = "PHPSESSID=$fields[1]";
            }
        }
        // decoding the JSON response
        try {
            $array = json_decode($json, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
        } catch (\JsonException) {
            $array = null;
        }
        if (!is_array($array) || !array_key_exists("response", $array)) {
            throw new TaxException("Invalid server response [$json]", 41);
        }
        // error?
        if ($statusCode !== 200) {
            // the message of the exception is the server's response completed by its HTTP status
            $message = json_encode(
                ["HTTP status" => $statusCode] + $array,
                JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR
            );
            throw new TaxException($message, 42);
        }
        // we return the useful element of the response
        return $array["response"];
    }

Comments

  • Line 71: The method is private. Its parameter is of type [ResponseInterface], the interface implemented by all responses from the Symfony client HTTP. Client PHP 7 used the type [CurlResponse], the response class when client HTTP is implemented with library [curl]: the [dao] layer was unnecessarily dependent on the implementation chosen by Symfony;
  • Lines 73–80: The response status, headers, and content are retrieved. The [false] parameter prevents Symfony from throwing an exception when the response status HTTP falls within the ranges [3xx, 4xx, 5xx]. If the server cannot be reached, Symfony throws a [TransportExceptionInterface] exception, which is converted to a [TaxException] exception with status code 40, as in previous versions;
  • lines 83–84: if in [$verbose] mode, the server’s response is displayed on the console;
  • lines 88–90: We retrieve the session cookie. Client PHP 7 only did this in the [initSession] method. We do this after every request because the server in version 12 changes the session cookie during the [end-session] action: it sends two headers, the first to delete the old cookie ([PHPSESSID=deleted]) and the second for the new one. The loop retains the last one. The regular expression [/^PHPSESSID=([^;]+)/] captures the cookie’s value up to the first semicolon, which separates the value from the cookie’s attributes (path, expires, etc.);
  • line 95: the string JSON is parsed into an array. The option [JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR] causes a [JsonException] exception to be thrown if the string is not a valid JSON;
  • lines 99–100: If the response is not a JSON object with the key [response], it is not a response from our web service. A code 41 exception is thrown;
  • Lines 103–109: If the status of the server’s response HTTP is not 200, an exception with code 42 is thrown; the exception message is the server’s response JSON, supplemented by the status HTTP, as with the previous clients. The [+] operator, when applied to two associative arrays, merges them: the [["HTTP status" => $statusCode]] array is populated with the keys [action, status, response] from the [$array] array;
  • Line 112: The relevant information is in [$array["response"]]. Depending on the action, this is a message, an associative array (a simulation), or a list of associative arrays (simulations). The method’s return type is therefore [mixed].

docs.title: The [authenticateUser] method
docs.text:
The [authenticateUser] method is as follows:

    // action [authenticate-user]
    #[\Override]
    public function authenticateUser(string $user, #[\SensitiveParameter] string $password): void
    {
        // POST main.php?action=authenticate-user with the posted parameters [user, password]
        $this->sendRequest(
            "POST",
            ["action" => "authenticate-user"],
            ["user" => $user, "password" => $password]
        );
    }

Comments

  • line 121: the client’s request is a POST;
  • line 122: the single parameter of the URL;
  • line 123: the parameters of the POST;
  • The response is not processed: we know that in the event of an error (HTTP code other than 200), the [getResponse] method itself throws an exception.

docs.title: The [calculateTax] method
docs.text:
// action [calculate-tax]
    #[\Override]
    public function calculateTax(string $married, int $children, int $salary): Simulation
    {
        // POST main.php?action=calculate-tax with the posted parameters [married, children, salary]
        $serverResponse = $this->sendRequest(
            "POST",
            ["action" => "calculate-tax"],
            ["married" => $married, "children" => $children, "salary" => $salary]
        );
        // the response is the array of the attributes of a simulation
        return self::toSimulation($serverResponse);
    }

Comments

  • line 134: the single parameter of URL;
  • line 135: the three parameters of POST;
  • line 138: if you reach this point, it means that the [getResponse] method did not throw an exception. The response is the associative array of a simulation’s attributes. The [toSimulation] method, described a little further on, converts it into a [Simulation] object.

docs.title: The [listSimulations] method
docs.text:
// action [list-simulations]
    #[\Override]
    public function listSimulations(): array
    {
        // GET main.php?action=list-simulations
        $serverResponse = $this->sendRequest("GET", ["action" => "list-simulations"]);
        // the response is a list of simulations
        return self::getSimulations($serverResponse);
    }

Comments

  • line 146: a GET request with the single parameter [action];
  • line 148: the transformation of the response into a list of [Simulation] objects is handled by the private method [getSimulations].

docs.title: The [getSimulations] method
docs.text:
// turns the list of associative arrays received from the server into a list of [Simulation] objects
    /** @return Simulation[] */
    private static function getSimulations(array $serverResponse): array
    {
        return array_map(self::toSimulation(...), $serverResponse);
    }

    // turns an associative array [married, children, salary, tax, ...] into a [Simulation] object
    private static function toSimulation(array $attributes): Simulation
    {
        // the keys of the array are the names of the parameters of the [Simulation] constructor
        return new Simulation(...$attributes);
    }

Comments

  • line 153: the method receives the response from the server, a list of associative arrays, each containing all the attributes of a simulation. It does not use any object attributes: it is static and called by [self::getSimulations(...)];
  • line 155: the function [array_map] applies the method [toSimulation] to each element of the list and returns the list of results. The syntax [self::toSimulation(...)] (PHP 8.1, “first-class callable syntax”) creates an anonymous function (a [Closure]) from the method [toSimulation]. It replaces the old syntax [[self::class, "toSimulation"]];
  • line 162: the [...] operator unpacks the [$attributes] array into constructor arguments. Starting with PHP 8.1, the string keys of the array become named arguments: the key [married] is passed to parameter [$married], the key [tax] to parameter [$tax], and so on, regardless of the order of the keys in the array. If the server sent a key unknown to the constructor, PHP would throw a [Error] error;
  • the client PHP 7 used the method [setFromArrayOfAttributes] of the class [BaseEntity] to initialize the object [Simulation] with the elements of the array. Note that the JSON serialization of its [Simulation] objects contained the redundant attribute [arrayOfAttributes] inherited from the [BaseEntity] class. This is no longer the case.

docs.title: The [deleteSimulation] method
docs.text:
// action [delete-simulation]
    #[\Override]
    public function deleteSimulation(int $number): array
    {
        // GET main.php?action=delete-simulation&number=1
        $serverResponse = $this->sendRequest("GET", ["action" => "delete-simulation", "number" => $number]);
        // the server returns the new list of the simulations
        return self::getSimulations($serverResponse);
    }

Comments

  • Line 170: A GET request is made with two parameters in the URL;
  • Line 172: After a deletion, the server returns the new list of simulations. This list is returned.

docs.title: The [endSession] method
docs.text:
A work session with the web service normally ends with a call to the [endSession] method:

    // action [end-session]
    #[\Override]
    public function endSession(): void
    {
        // GET main.php?action=end-session - the response is a simple message
        $this->sendRequest("GET", ["action" => "end-session"]);
    }

Comments

  • Line 180: A request is made to GET with the single parameter [action]. An exception will be thrown if the response status code HTTP is not 200. The server responds with a new session cookie that the [getResponse] method stores: subsequent requests will be made within the new session, where the user is not authenticated.

docs.title: 23.14.3.1. The interface
docs.text:
The interface of the [business] layer is as follows: [Business/InterfaceClientBusiness.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the interface of the [business] layer of the client of the JSON web service of version 12
interface InterfaceClientBusiness
{
    // calculation of the taxes in batch mode: the only method specific to the [business] layer
    // the results are only saved if [$resultsFileName] is not null
    public function executeBatchTaxes(
        string $taxPayersFileName,
        string $errorsFileName,
        ?string $resultsFileName = null
    ): void;

    // the following methods are those of the [dao] layer
    // calculation of the tax of a taxpayer
    public function calculateTax(string $married, int $children, int $salary): Simulation;

    // saving the results
    /** @param Simulation[] $simulations */
    public function saveResults(string $resultsFilename, array $simulations): void;

    // start of session
    public function initSession(string $type = "json"): void;

    // authentication
    public function authenticateUser(string $user, #[\SensitiveParameter] string $password): void;

    // list of the simulations
    /** @return Simulation[] */
    public function listSimulations(): array;

    // deletion of a simulation
    /** @return Simulation[] */
    public function deleteSimulation(int $number): array;

    // end of session
    public function endSession(): void;
}

Comments

  • line 13: Only the method [executeBatchTaxes] is specific to the [business] layer. All others belong to the [dao] layer, which implements them;
  • Line 16: The results file is optional. If it is missing, the results are not saved. The parameter is of type [?string] (string or [null]). We placed it last: an optional parameter must follow the required parameters. Course PHP 7 declared [string $resultsFileName] and passed [NULL] to the method, which causes a [TypeError]-type error in [strict_types=1] mode.

docs.title: 23.14.3.2. The [ClientBusiness] class
docs.text:
The class implementing the [business] layer is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the [business] layer of the client: the tax calculation is done by the server
class ClientBusiness implements InterfaceClientBusiness
{
    // the [dao] layer is injected by the constructor
    public function __construct(private readonly InterfaceClientDao $clientDao)
    {
    }

    // calculation of the taxes in batch mode
    #[\Override]
    public function executeBatchTaxes(
        string $taxPayersFileName,
        string $errorsFileName,
        ?string $resultsFileName = null
    ): void {
        // we let the exceptions coming from the [dao] layer go up
        // we retrieve the taxpayers data
        $taxPayersData = $this->clientDao->getTaxPayersData($taxPayersFileName, $errorsFileName);
        // we calculate the tax of each taxpayer: the server stores the simulations in the session
        $simulations = array_map(
            fn(TaxPayerData $taxPayerData): Simulation => $this->calculateTax(
                $taxPayerData->married,
                $taxPayerData->children,
                $taxPayerData->salary
            ),
            $taxPayersData
        );
        // saving the results, if requested
        if ($resultsFileName !== null) {
            $this->clientDao->saveResults($resultsFileName, $simulations);
        }
    }

    // the other methods delegate the work to the [dao] layer
    #[\Override]
    public function calculateTax(string $married, int $children, int $salary): Simulation
    {
        return $this->clientDao->calculateTax($married, $children, $salary);
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function saveResults(string $resultsFilename, array $simulations): void
    {
        $this->clientDao->saveResults($resultsFilename, $simulations);
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function initSession(string $type = "json"): void
    {
        $this->clientDao->initSession($type);
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function authenticateUser(string $user, #[\SensitiveParameter] string $password): void
    {
        $this->clientDao->authenticateUser($user, $password);
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function listSimulations(): array
    {
        return $this->clientDao->listSimulations();
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function deleteSimulation(int $number): array
    {
        return $this->clientDao->deleteSimulation($number);
    }

    #[\Override]
    public function endSession(): void
    {
        $this->clientDao->endSession();
    }
}

Comments

  • line 12: To be instantiated, the [business] layer requires a reference to the [dao] layer. This reference is injected by the constructor and becomes a read-only attribute through parameter promotion;
  • Lines 18–22: Only the [executeBatchTaxes] method is specific to the [business] layer. The implementations of the other methods delegate the work to the methods of the same names in the [dao] layer;
  • line 25: the [dao] layer is accessed to retrieve taxpayer data into an array of objects of type [TaxPayerData];
  • Lines 27–34: The tax for each taxpayer in the [$taxPayersData] array is calculated. The arrow function (PHP 7.4) called by [array_map] returns, for each taxpayer, the [Simulation] object returned by the server. Each calculation is also stored by the server in the user’s session;
  • lines 36–37: the results are saved to a JSON file only if a filename has been specified.

Note: The [business] layer does virtually nothing. One might decide to remove it and consolidate everything into the [dao] layer.

docs.title: 23.14.4. The main script
docs.text:
The main script is configured by the following file, [Data/config.json]:

{
    "urlServer": "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/main.php",
    "user": {
        "login": "admin",
        "passwd": "admin"
    },
    "httpClientOptions": {
        "verify_peer": false,
        "verify_host": false
    },
    "taxPayersDataFilename": "Data/taxpayersdata.json",
    "resultsFilename": "Data/results.json",
    "errorsFilename": "Data/errors.json",
    "dependencies": [
        "../version-05/Entities/TaxException.php",
        "../version-05/Entities/TaxPayerData.php",
        "../version-05/Utilities/Utilities.php",
        "../version-05/Dao/TraitDao.php",
        "../../../scripts-web/tax/version-12/Entities/Simulation.php",
        "Dao/InterfaceClientDao.php",
        "Dao/ClientDao.php",
        "Business/InterfaceClientBusiness.php",
        "Business/ClientBusiness.php"
    ]
}
  • Line 2: the URL for the main server controller in version 12. We use the [http] schema, as we have since version 8 (see the section “Why [http] and not [https]?” in the chapter on version 8);
  • line 3: the user’s credentials;
  • line 7: the HTTP client options, already used by the Version 11 client: if URL uses the [https] schema, the server’s self-signed certificate is not verified;
  • Lines 14–24: The application files to be loaded, related to the client's [version-12] folder. This includes the server’s [Simulation] class. Course PHP 7 also provided an absolute root directory, [rootDirectory], and the absolute path to the Composer autoloader. As with previous versions, the paths are now calculated based on the constant [__DIR__]: the [php8-oct-2026] folder can be moved without changing the configuration.

The main script [Main/main.php] is as follows:

<?php

// strict respect of the declared types of function parameters and results
declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the root folder of the client: the paths of the configuration file are relative to this folder
const ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__ . "/..";
// path of the configuration file
const CONFIG_FILENAME = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Data/config.json";

// we retrieve the configuration
$config = json_decode(file_get_contents(CONFIG_FILENAME), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);

// we include the dependencies needed by the script: third-party libraries (Symfony) then application files
require_once ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/../../../vendor/autoload.php";
foreach ($config["dependencies"] as $dependency) {
    require_once ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/$dependency";
}

// the paths of the data files
$taxPayersDataFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["taxPayersDataFilename"];
$resultsFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["resultsFilename"];
$errorsFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["errorsFilename"];

// creation of the [dao] layer - the server's responses will be displayed (verbose)
$clientDao = new ClientDao($config["urlServer"], $config["httpClientOptions"], verbose: true);
// creation of the [business] layer
$clientBusiness = new ClientBusiness($clientDao);

// a complete dialogue with the JSON web service
try {
    // initialization of a JSON session
    $clientBusiness->initSession("json");
    // authentication
    $clientBusiness->authenticateUser($config["user"]["login"], $config["user"]["passwd"]);
    // calculation of the taxes in batch mode, without saving the results (no [resultsFileName] parameter)
    $clientBusiness->executeBatchTaxes(
        taxPayersFileName: $taxPayersDataFilename,
        errorsFileName: $errorsFilename
    );
    // list of the simulations
    $clientBusiness->listSimulations();
    // deletion of the simulation no. 1 (the 2nd one of the list)
    $simulations = $clientBusiness->deleteSimulation(1);
    // saving the remaining simulations
    $clientBusiness->saveResults($resultsFilename, $simulations);
    print count($simulations) . " simulations have been saved in the file [{$config["resultsFilename"]}]\n";
    // end of session
    $clientBusiness->endSession();
    // action in the new session, where we are not authenticated: must fail
    $clientBusiness->listSimulations();
} catch (TaxException $ex) {
    // we display the error
    print "Error no. {$ex->getCode()}: {$ex->getMessage()}\n";
}
// end
print "Done\n";

Comments

  • lines 10–15: processing the configuration file [config.json];
  • lines 18–20: loading all dependencies;
  • lines 24–26: absolute paths to the data files;
  • lines 29–31: building the layers [dao] and [business]. The parameter [$verbose] is passed by name: [verbose: true] is more descriptive than simply [true];
  • line 36: initialization of a JSON session;
  • line 38: authenticating with the server;
  • lines 40–43: calculating the tax for a group of taxpayers. The results are not saved: thanks to named arguments, we simply omit the optional parameter [resultsFileName];
  • line 45: the results of all these calculations are retrieved;
  • line 47: delete simulation #1 (the second one on the list);
  • line 49: Save the remaining simulations;
  • line 52: the session is ended. The server deletes the session and starts a new one;
  • line 54: the list of simulations is requested. In the new session, the user is not authenticated. Therefore, an exception should occur indicating that the user is not authenticated.

docs.title: 23.14.5. [PHPUnit] Tests
docs.text:
As with previous clients, the Version 12 client can be tested using [PHPUnit]. The test class [Tests/ClientBusinessTest.php] is similar to that of previous clients:

<?php

// strict respect of the declared types of function parameters and results
declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace of the tests
namespace Application\Tests;

// the tested classes
use Application\ClientDao;
use Application\ClientBusiness;
use Application\TaxException;
use Application\InterfaceClientBusiness;
use Application\Simulation;
// the PHPUnit classes
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

// test of the [business] layer of the client of the JSON web service: the server must be running
final class ClientBusinessTest extends TestCase
{
    // the root folder of the client
    private const string ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__ . "/..";
    // the configuration of the client
    private static array $config;
    // the tested [business] layer
    private InterfaceClientBusiness $business;

    // executed once, before the first test of the class
    #[\Override]
    public static function setUpBeforeClass(): void
    {
        // we retrieve the configuration of the client
        self::$config = json_decode(file_get_contents(self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Data/config.json"), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
        // we include the dependencies of the client (the Composer autoloader is already loaded by PHPUnit)
        foreach (self::$config["dependencies"] as $dependency) {
            require_once self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/$dependency";
        }
    }

    // executed before each test: each test has its own authenticated JSON session
    #[\Override]
    protected function setUp(): void
    {
        // creation of the [dao] (non-verbose) and [business] layers
        $clientDao = new ClientDao(self::$config["urlServer"], self::$config["httpClientOptions"], verbose: false);
        $this->business = new ClientBusiness($clientDao);
        // initialization of a JSON session
        $this->business->initSession("json");
        // authentication
        $this->business->authenticateUser(self::$config["user"]["login"], self::$config["user"]["passwd"]);
    }

    // the taxpayers of the table of official figures
    public static function taxpayers(): array
    {
        // [married, children, salary, official tax, expected [tax, surcharge, discount, reduction, rate]]
        return [
            "couple, 2 children, 55555" => ["yes", 2, 55555, 2815, [2814, 0, 0, 0, 0.14]],
            "couple, 2 children, 50000" => ["yes", 2, 50000, 1385, [1384, 0, 384, 347, 0.14]],
            "couple, 3 children, 50000" => ["yes", 3, 50000, 0, [0, 0, 720, 0, 0.14]],
            "single, 2 children, 100000" => ["no", 2, 100000, 19884, [19884, 4480, 0, 0, 0.41]],
            "single, 3 children, 100000" => ["no", 3, 100000, 16782, [16782, 7176, 0, 0, 0.41]],
            "couple, 3 children, 100000" => ["yes", 3, 100000, 9200, [9200, 2180, 0, 0, 0.3]],
            "couple, 5 children, 100000" => ["yes", 5, 100000, 4230, [4230, 0, 0, 0, 0.14]],
            "single, 0 children, 100000" => ["no", 0, 100000, 22986, [22986, 0, 0, 0, 0.41]],
            "couple, 2 children, 30000" => ["yes", 2, 30000, 0, [0, 0, 0, 0, 0.0]],
            "single, 0 children, 200000" => ["no", 0, 200000, 64211, [64210, 7498, 0, 0, 0.45]],
            "couple, 3 children, 200000" => ["yes", 3, 200000, 42843, [42842, 17283, 0, 0, 0.41]],
        ];
    }

    // a test executed once for each of the taxpayers of the data provider
    #[DataProvider("taxpayers")]
    public function testCalculateTax(string $married, int $children, int $salary, int $officialTax, array $expected): void
    {
        // tax calculation
        $simulation = $this->business->calculateTax($married, $children, $salary);
        // the tax is the one of the official simulator to within 1 euro
        $this->assertEqualsWithDelta($officialTax, $simulation->tax, 1);
        // the simulation is exactly the expected one: [assertEquals] compares the attributes of the two objects
        $this->assertEquals(new Simulation($married, $children, $salary, ...$expected), $simulation);
    }

    // the [list-simulations] and [delete-simulation] actions
    public function testListDeleteSimulations(): void
    {
        // two simulations in a new session
        $this->business->calculateTax("yes", 2, 55555);
        $this->business->calculateTax("no", 0, 100000);
        $this->assertCount(2, $this->business->listSimulations());
        // deletion of the 1st one: the second one remains
        $simulations = $this->business->deleteSimulation(0);
        $this->assertCount(1, $simulations);
        $this->assertSame(22986, $simulations[0]->tax);
        // the simulation no. 1 no longer exists: status 628, HTTP status 400
        $this->assertError(400, 628, fn() => $this->business->deleteSimulation(1));
    }

    // after the end of the session, the user is no longer authenticated
    public function testEndSession(): void
    {
        $this->business->endSession();
        // status 104: action requested by an unauthenticated user
        $this->assertError(400, 104, fn() => $this->business->listSimulations());
    }

    // checks that the action [$action] throws a [TaxException] exception with code 42
    // whose JSON message contains the expected HTTP status and status
    private function assertError(int $httpStatus, int $status, \Closure $action): void
    {
        try {
            $action();
            $this->fail("a [TaxException] exception was expected");
        } catch (TaxException $ex) {
            $this->assertSame(42, $ex->getCode());
            $error = json_decode($ex->getMessage(), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
            $this->assertSame($httpStatus, $error["HTTP status"]);
            $this->assertSame($status, $error["status"]);
        }
    }
}

Comments

  • lines 31–37: The client configuration is read and dependencies are loaded only once, before the first test;
  • Lines 43–51: Note that the [setUp] method is executed before each test. It constructs the layers [dao] (in non-verbose mode) and [business], then initializes a session JSON and authenticates itself. Each test thus runs in its own session, independent of the other tests. Course PHP 7 performed this task in the test class constructor, which PHPUnit no longer allows;
  • lines 55–69: the data provider from previous versions. For each taxpayer, we have the tax calculated by the official simulator and the five expected results from [tax, surcharge, discount, reduction, rate];
  • line 82: the expected simulation is constructed and compared to the one returned by the server. When applied to two objects, the [assertEquals] method verifies that they are of the same class and that their attributes are equal. The operator [...] decomposes a list here: its elements are passed to the last five parameters of the constructor, in order;
  • Lines 86–97: A test of the actions [list-simulations] and [delete-simulation]. We run two simulations, delete the first one, and verify that the second one remains. Then we request the deletion of a simulation that does not exist: the server must respond with status 628;
  • lines 101–105: After the session ends, the list of simulations must be rejected with status code 104;
  • lines 110–119: a utility method that verifies that the action [$action], passed as an anonymous function, throws a [TaxException] exception with code 42, the expected status HTTP, and the expected status. Since the exception message is the server’s JSON response, it is decoded to verify its elements. If no exception is thrown, the [fail] method causes the test to fail.

The test results are as follows:

> php vendor/bin/phpunit scripts-console/tax/version-12/Tests --testdox
PHPUnit 12.5.37 by Sebastian Bergmann and contributors.

Runtime:       PHP 8.5.11
Configuration: .../php8-oct-2026/phpunit.xml

.............                                                     13 / 13 (100%)

Time: 00:00.195, Memory: 16.00 MB

Client Business (Application\Tests\ClientBusiness)
 ✔ Calculate tax with data set "couple, 2 children, 55555"
 ✔ Calculate tax with data set "couple, 2 children, 50000"
 ✔ Calculate tax with data set "couple, 3 children, 50000"
 ✔ Calculate tax with data set "single, 2 children, 100000"
 ✔ Calculate tax with data set "single, 3 children, 100000"
 ✔ Calculate tax with data set "couple, 3 children, 100000"
 ✔ Calculate tax with data set "couple, 5 children, 100000"
 ✔ Calculate tax with data set "single, 0 children, 100000"
 ✔ Calculate tax with data set "couple, 2 children, 30000"
 ✔ Calculate tax with data set "single, 0 children, 200000"
 ✔ Calculate tax with data set "couple, 3 children, 200000"
 ✔ List delete simulations
 ✔ End session

OK (13 tests, 31 assertions)

Many other tests should be performed:

  • test the various methods of the [dao] layer;
  • test the status codes returned by the web server. These status codes are important because their values determine which HTML page to display.

docs.title: 24. Practical Exercise – Version 13
docs.text: Version 13 introduces few changes: it secures access to the application’s files. It adds no new features: the actions, the responses JSON, XML, and HTML, and the views are the same as in version 12. What has changed is the file structure on the disk and the configuration of the [Apache] server.

docs.title: 24.1. The Problem
docs.text:
In Course PHP 7, you could request the URL of the version 12 configuration file, and the browser would display it. However, this [config.json] file contains sensitive information, such as the credentials of users authorized to use the application. It must not be accessible to users.

In our version 12, this file is already protected: it is located in the [Data] folder, to which the [.htaccess] file—introduced with version 8—denies access ([Require all denied] directive). However, this protection is applied on a case-by-case basis: we block only what we’ve specifically chosen to block, and everything else is served. Yet there are still many things that should not be displayed. For example, the browser may request a view directly, without going through the main controller:

> curl -i http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/Views/view-tax-calculation.php
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: Apache/2.4.58
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Vary: Accept-Encoding
Content-Length: 1017
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8

<br />
<b>Warning</b>:  Undefined variable $request in <b>.../php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/Views/view-tax-calculation.php</b> on line <b>9</b><br />
<br />
<b>Warning</b>:  Undefined variable $content in <b>.../php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/Views/view-tax-calculation.php</b> on line <b>9</b><br />
<br />
<b>Fatal error</b>:  Uncaught TypeError: getModelForThisView(): Argument #1 ($request) must be of type Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request, null given, called in .../php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/Views/view-tax-calculation.php on line 9 and defined in .../php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/Views/view-tax-calculation.php:11
Stack trace:
#0 .../php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/Views/view-tax-calculation.php(9): getModelForThisView(NULL, NULL)
#1 {main}
  thrown in <b>.../php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/tax/version-12/Views/view-tax-calculation.php</b> on line <b>11</b><br />

The view is executed out of context: the variables normally provided by the [HtmlResponse] class do not exist. Since [Laragon] is configured for development (directive [display_errors=On] from PHP), error messages are sent to the browser. They reveal the file paths on the server, as well as the names of the functions and classes used—all of which is useful information for anyone seeking to attack the application. Secondary controllers, response classes, and the classes in the [business] and [dao] layers can likewise be executed by a simple URL. Here, they merely define a class, but there is no guarantee that this will always be the case.

More seriously: the entire [php8-oct-2026] folder for the course is located inside the [www] folder of [Laragon]. The console script files are also accessible via the web, even though no one thought to protect them:

> curl -i http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-console/tax/version-05/Data/database.json

    "colHalfShareReductionValue": "halfShareReductionValue",
    "colSingleDiscountCeiling": "singleDiscountCeiling",

    "colSingleTaxCeilingForDiscount": "singleTaxCeilingForDiscount",
    "colCoupleTaxCeilingForDiscount": "coupleTaxCeilingForDiscount",
    "colTenPercentAllowanceMax": "tenPercentAllowanceMax",
    "colTenPercentAllowanceMin": "tenPercentAllowanceMin"
}

Anyone can read the username and password for the [dbtaxes-2019] database user. However, server versions 8 through 12 use this file or its equivalent.

The correct approach is the opposite: block everything by default, then explicitly allow only what needs to be accessible from the outside. For our application, only three files need to be accessible:

  • [main.php], the main controller, which receives all requests;
  • [index.php], the entry point for the application HTML, which redirects to [main.php];
  • the image [logo.jpg], which the browser requests via a HTTP request when it displays the view banner.

docs.title: 24.2. The new directory structure
docs.text:
We copy and paste the [scripts-web/tax/version-12] folder into [scripts-web/tax/version-13], then reorganize its files:

scripts-web/tax/version-13

├── Config
│   ├── config.json
│   ├── database.json
│   └── vhost-tax-v13.conf
├── Controllers
│   └── (the secondary controllers of version 12)
├── Entities
│   ├── Action.php
│   ├── ControllerResult.php
│   ├── Database.php
│   ├── ResponseType.php
│   ├── Simulation.php
│   ├── TaxAdminData.php
│   └── TaxException.php
├── Logs
│   └── logs.txt
├── Model
│   ├── InterfaceServerBusiness.php
│   ├── InterfaceServerDao.php
│   ├── ServerBusiness.php
│   ├── ServerDao.php
│   └── ServerDaoWithSession.php
├── Responses
│   └── (the response classes of version 12)
├── Utilities
│   ├── Logger.php
│   ├── SendAdminMail.php
│   ├── Utilities.php
│   └── XmlUtilities.php
├── Views
│   └── (the views of version 12, without the logo)
└── public
    ├── Resources
    │   └── logo.jpg
    ├── index.php
    └── main.php
  • into [public], the only folder that will be accessible via the web. It contains the two scripts [index.php, main.php] and, in the [Resources] folder, the image [logo.jpg]. The name [public] is the one used by current PHP frameworks (Symfony, Laravel) for this same role;
  • In [Config], the configuration files: [config.json] (formerly [Data/config.json]) and [database.json], and the database configuration that was taken from the [Data] folder in version 8. The file [vhost-tax-v13.conf] will be presented at the end of the chapter;
  • in [Logs], the log file, which was in the [Data] folder;
  • and in [Model], the layer classes [business] and [dao] from the server. Until now, they were loaded from the version 8 and 9 folders. They have now been copied to the version 13 folder, along with the features [TaxException, TaxAdminData, Database] (version 5) and the utilities [Logger, SendAdminMail] (version 9), [XmlUtilities] (version 11), and [Utilities] (version 5). The [version-13] folder thus contains the entire application: this is the only folder that would be copied to a production server, without relying on folders from other versions;
  • the [Tests] folder from version 12, which contained the test pages for the views, is not included: these pages would no longer be accessible via the web anyway.

The names of these files do not change, nor does their content, with three exceptions that we will now discuss. Only the Composer library [vendor] remains in its original location, at the root of the [php8-oct-2026] folder.

docs.title: 24.3.2. The main controller [public/main.php]
docs.text:
The main controller has been moved to the [public] folder. Only two lines have changed:

// PHP errors are not sent to the client (they go to the web server's log)
ini_set("display_errors", "0");

// the application's root folder, parent of the [public] folder: the paths of the configuration file are relative to this folder
const ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__ . "/..";
// path of the configuration file
const CONFIG_FILENAME = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Config/config.json";

// Composer's autoloader (Symfony, Predis)
require_once ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/../../../vendor/autoload.php";
  • Line 18: The constant [ROOT_DIRECTORY] still refers to the application’s root folder, relative to which the paths in the [config.json] file are defined. Since the script is now in the [public] folder, this root folder is the parent folder of [__DIR__]. You cannot write [dirname(__DIR__)]: the value of a constant declared with [const] must be a constant expression, and a function call is not one. The concatenation of [__DIR__] (a constant) and a string is a constant expression;
  • line 20: the new path to the configuration file;
  • line 23: this line does not change: the path to the Composer loader is relative to the application’s root directory, which is always [scripts-web/tax/version-13].

The script [public/index.php] is the one from version 12. Its redirection to the relative path URL via [main.php?action=init-session&type=html] remains correct since [index.php] and [main.php] are in the same folder.
